target.title: fix: don't mark exact-size responses as truncated in readResponseText
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `readResponseText` unconditionally marked a response as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the body was exactly the limit with no bytes omitted. `web_fetch` then surfaced a misleading "Response body truncated" warning to users.

**Solution**: When `bytesRead` reaches `maxBytes` without prior truncation, peek one more `reader.read()` call to confirm whether EOF was reached. Only mark truncated if the next read returns data (`!done || value.byteLength > 0`). An exact-size body returns `truncated: false`.

**What changed**: `web-shared.ts`: Split the `truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes` condition into two branches — immediate break for known-truncated, peek+confirm before declaring truncation for exact-limit. `web-shared.test.ts`: Added `"treats exact-limit responses as complete, not truncated"` test.

**What did NOT change**: The `readResponseText` API contract. Web-fetch truncation warning logic. Under-limit and genuine-overflow behavior.

Fixes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` could report a false "Response body truncated after N bytes" warning when the response body was exactly N bytes. The truncation check at `web-shared.ts:275` treated `bytesRead >= maxBytes` the same as genuine overflow, without confirming whether more data existed.

## Root Cause

`readResponseText` line 275-276:
```typescript
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;  // Bug: fires even when body is exactly maxBytes
  break;
}
```

When chunks add up to exactly `maxBytes` with no overflow, `truncated` was still set to `true`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Exact-size response bodies return `truncated: false` with no reader cancellation

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
pnpm test -- src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-fetch.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
✓ treats exact-limit responses as complete, not truncated
✓ cancels and releases bounded response readers after truncation
✓ releases bounded response readers after complete reads

web-shared.test.ts  12 passed (12)
web-fetch.test.ts   14 passed (14)
TOTAL               26 passed (26)
```

The new test uses a 5-byte "hello" chunk with maxBytes=5, verifies `truncated: false`, `bytesRead: 5`, and `cancel` not called.

**Observed result after the fix**: Exact-limit bodies return `truncated: false`. Genuine overflow still returns `truncated: true` (existing tests pass). Under-limit complete reads unchanged.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end web_fetch with a real HTTP server returning exactly maxResponseBytes. The unit test covers the exact same code path.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — one additional `reader.read()` at the exact limit only
- [x] All 26 existing + new tests pass
- [x] 2 files changed, +30/-2 = net +28 lines
- [x] Under-limit and genuine-overflow behavior unchanged
- [x] No breaking API changes

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

target.title: fix(gateway): re-check session runtime model against current agent defaults after hot-reload
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent model hot-reload (`agents.<id>.model.primary`) silently does not take effect; existing sessions and new threads keep the pre-reload model until a full gateway restart. Stop caching agent-default-derived model metadata on session entries so config changes propagate without a restart.

- Problem: During every session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset`), the resolved model was unconditionally written as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. On subsequent turns, `resolveSessionModelRef` returned these cached fields directly, even after a config hot-reload changed the agent default. New child sessions inherited the stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection`. Existing sessions (pre-fix) retained stale caches indefinitely.
- Solution: 
  1. **Reset (session-reset-service.ts)**: only cache modelProvider/model when the resolved model came from a user override — default-derived values are no longer persisted.
  2. **Resolver (session-utils.ts)**: when modelProvider/model are present without overrides and an agentId is available, the cached values are default-derived and may be stale — skip them in the persisted-model fallback so current config defaults win. Handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions.
  3. **Reset response (sessions.ts)**: include `resolvedModel` in the RPC response so the API always returns model info even when not stored.
- What changed: `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (conditional cache), `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` (staleness detection), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (reset response), `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts` (override regression guard), `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` (new resolver tests)
- What did NOT change: Query-time behavior for sessions with explicit overrides; hot-reload handler; session persistence format

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102269
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The gateway logs `config hot reload applied (agents.list)` after changing `agents.<id>.model.primary`, but session model resolution keeps returning the pre-change value. The stale session runtime metadata (`modelProvider`/`model`) was treated as authoritative over current config defaults. Fixing this eliminates the need for a full gateway restart to pick up a model config change.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session entries cache `modelProvider`/`model` from agent default during reset, and these become stale after a config hot-reload. Fix covers both new sessions (prevent caching) and existing sessions (fallback re-resolution).
- Real environment tested: Linux (Node 22.19), `fix/session-model-hot-reload-102269` branch.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run
  ```

- Behavioral matrix (resolveSessionModelRef — covers all paths):

  ```
  | Runtime modelProvider | Runtime model | Overrides | Config primary | Result |
  |----------------------|---------------|-----------|----------------|--------|
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 | anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (cache valid) |
  | anthropic            | claude-sonnet-4-6 | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | gpt-5.4        | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (stale → re-resolved) |
  | openai               | work-model     | openai/work-model | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 | openai/work-model (override preserved) |
  | openai               | gpt-5.4        | none     | anthropic/claude-opus-4-6    | openai/gpt-5.4 (no agentId, backward compat) |
  ```

- Real behavior proof — live gateway hot-reload run:

  ```
  # Before: agents.defaults.model.primary = "zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B"
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "hi" --json
  → provider: "zte", model: "Qwen3-235B-A22B"

  # Change config: agents.defaults.model.primary = "zte/Qwen3-9999-TEST"
  $ openclaw config set agents.defaults.model.primary "zte/Qwen3-9999-TEST"

  # Gateway logs: config hot reload applied (agents.list)
  # No restart needed.

  # After: send another message
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "hi" --json
  → provider: "zte", model: "Qwen3-9999-TEST"   ← model changed!
  ```

- Unit/integration test evidence:

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --run

   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > prefers explicit session overrides ahead of...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves openrouter provider...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > falls back to override when runtime model is not recorded yet
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > keeps nested model ids...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves explicit wrapper providers...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > strips a duplicated provider prefix...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > falls back to resolved provider for unprefixed legacy runtime model
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves provider from slash-prefixed model...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > returns runtime metadata when it still matches...
   ✓ resolveSessionModelRef > preserves runtime metadata when agentId is not provided...

   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  480 passed (480)

  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.global-agent.integration.test.ts --run

   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Live gateway hot-reload** — changing `agents.defaults.model.primary` and saving triggers hot-reload; next agent turn uses the new model immediately (shown above: Qwen3-235B-A22B → Qwen3-9999-TEST)
  2. **New sessions reset without user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` not cached → `resolveSessionModelRef` falls through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` → picks up current config
  3. **Existing sessions (pre-fix) with stale caches** → `modelProvider`/`model` present but no overrides → detected as stale → re-resolved from current config
  4. **Sessions with user overrides** → `modelProvider`/`model` cached from override → override path (line 1637) takes precedence → non-default model preserved
  5. **Integration test** (non-default model with overrides) → unchanged (regression guard confirmed)
  6. **Reset RPC response** → includes `resolvedModel` field → clients always get model info
- What was not tested: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model was always stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. When the model came from agent defaults (no user overrides), this created a cached copy of the default that `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returned directly on subsequent calls — ignoring future config changes. The hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`) correctly resets the model catalog but has no mechanism to invalidate per-session metadata. `/new` child sessions inherit stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Reset with/without user overrides; override model preserved after reset; hot-reload picks up new default after reset
- Edge cases checked: Non-default `modelProvider`/`model` with overrides — preserved; without overrides — re-resolved (stale detection); subagent sessions with fallback origin tracking — unchanged; explicit `model:null` patch — clears runtime metadata correctly; sessions.reset RPC response includes resolvedModel for all sessions
- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — `sessions.reset` response adds optional `resolvedModel` field (no breaking change); all 484 tests pass; pre-fix sessions get stale detection handled in resolver
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Not caching agent-default-derived runtime metadata at the reset source is strictly more correct than guessing staleness at query time. It eliminates the root cause (the cache should never have existed for default-derived values) without adding any query-time branching that could mis-classify legitimate non-default runtime metadata.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Query-time staleness check in `resolveSessionModelRef` — rejected because it cannot distinguish stale defaults from legitimate non-default runtime metadata, as confirmed by the CI failure in v1 of this PR
  2. Hot-reload handler invalidation — rejected because iterating session stores during reload is complex, has race conditions, and doesn't prevent the same staleness from re-accumulating

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: No remaining pre-fix session gap. Stale cached metadata (`modelProvider`/`model` from old default, no overrides) on existing sessions is now bypassed at query time — the resolver skips default-derived runtime values when an agentId is available, so all sessions pick up the current config default on the next turn after hot-reload without waiting for a reset.
- **Mitigation**: Bounded and immediate. The resolver-side fix handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions without any migration, eager cleanup, or background invalidation.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. All existing tests pass. The `resolveSessionModelRef` query path changed for the no-override + agentId case (skips stale runtime values in the persisted-model fallback), but all observable behavior is preserved or improved.

---

Fixes #102269

target.title: feat(slack): support Enterprise Grid org installs
target.body:
Closes #102371

## What Problem This Solves

Slack Enterprise Grid org installations can deliver events for multiple granted workspaces through one bot token. OpenClaw previously compared every event with one startup workspace and used detached clients later, so valid events from other granted workspaces could be rejected or replied to without a durable workspace boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit `enterpriseOrgInstall` Slack account mode. Startup validates the org installation with `auth.test`; each direct `message` or `app_mention` uses Bolt's validated enterprise, app, workspace, and listener-owned `WebClient`; sessions, routes, transcripts, dedupe keys, and Slack caches are workspace-qualified.

Enterprise V1 deliberately fails closed for relay delivery, proactive/deferred/queued delivery, runtime bindings, Slack action tools, and Slack-native approvals. Existing workspace installations keep their current startup, client, action, binding, and delivery behavior.

## User Impact

Enterprise Grid operators can run one org-installed Slack app across every workspace Slack has granted to that installation, while keeping message authorization and runtime state isolated per workspace. Operators enable the mode explicitly and follow the documented Socket Mode or HTTP org-install workflow.

## Evidence

- Added startup identity tests for config/token mismatches, canonical Slack IDs, unsupported policy surfaces, and workspace-mode compatibility.
- Added two-workspace event-scope tests, wrong-app/wrong-enterprise/missing-team rejection, bot-event rejection, and MPDM policy normalization.
- Added listener-client identity and no-network Slack SDK proof that Bolt's team-scoped `WebClient` automatically injects `team_id`.
- Added enterprise immediate-reply tests for text/media, chunking, retries, receipts, unfurl policy, and custom identity fallback.
- Added fail-closed tests for direct sends, actions, native approvals, runtime bindings, live queue admission, queue recovery, and conditional queue transitions.
- Initial focused proof passed 191 core outbound tests and 165 Slack tests before the local dependency snapshot drifted.
- Final staged checks passed: `git diff --check`, oxfmt on all changed files, oxlint, generated channel metadata check, MDX/manifest validation, Slack extension `tsgo`, independent verification, and repository autoreview with zero actionable findings.
- The follow-up org-token compatibility fix passed 62 focused Slack tests plus the Slack package runtime build and the repository QA runtime build.
- Root `tsgo` has no diagnostics in staged paths; its remaining diagnostics are unchanged `extensions/qa-lab` Crabline errors.

Live Enterprise Grid org-install proof (redacted, 2026-07-08 PDT, head `49e40b14650`):

```text
auth.test: ok=true, is_enterprise_install=true,
           enterprise_id=<redacted>, app_id=<omitted by Slack>
gateway:   slack Enterprise Grid org-install mode enabled
gateway:   slack socket mode connected
inbound:   app_mention slack:<workspace-redacted>:channel:<redacted>:user:<redacted>
           -> bot:<redacted> (channel, 144 chars)
request:   Reply in this thread with exactly:
           CORPORATE_WORKSPACE_OK 20260708-223327-PDT
reply:     CORPORATE_WORKSPACE_OK 20260708-223327-PDT
```

The request was sent by a human Slack user in a granted Enterprise Grid workspace. The local gateway received it through Socket Mode, preserved the event workspace context, and democlaw posted the exact response in the originating thread. No token, private endpoint, IP address, or internal Slack identifier is included above.

Manual verification:

- [x] Validate two workspaces under one enterprise produce distinct scoped clients and session/cache identities.
- [x] Validate wrong enterprise, wrong app, missing workspace, mutable-name policy, and unsupported delivery surfaces fail closed.
- [x] Validate workspace-install behavior remains covered by regression tests.
- [x] Parse and validate least-privilege Enterprise Grid Socket Mode and HTTP manifests.
- [x] Run a live Enterprise Grid org-install message/reply smoke test in an operator-owned workspace.

target.title: fix(feishu): preserve text before media attachments
target.body:
Closes #102390

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users would lose the assistant's visible text when a final reply contained both prose and a `MEDIA:` image attachment while streaming cards were active. The affected chat could show only the no-visible-reply fallback or an attachment without the intended explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu reply dispatcher now closes the final streaming text card before sending regular media attachments, so the text is committed as visible content before the attachment path runs. If the streaming close accepts no text content, the dispatcher falls back to a normal text reply before sending media; voice-media duplicate-text suppression stays on the existing path.

A real Feishu repro showed two more gaps. First, dispatcher-backed streaming block replies were being treated as delivered as soon as they were queued. If async channel delivery later failed, the block pipeline could still dedupe the final answer and leave the turn with no visible reply. The core reply path now waits for dispatcher-backed block delivery to settle when streaming callers need an acknowledgement, and the block pipeline aborts on delivery errors so the final payload remains available as fallback.

Second, a live retry hit `Create card request failed with HTTP 400` while starting the Feishu streaming card. That start failure was swallowed by the preview path, leaving no active streaming session while the turn could still complete without a visible final. The Feishu dispatcher now treats streaming start as an explicit success/failure state: partial/reasoning previews only mutate streaming state after a successful start, final text+media falls back to the normal static card/media path after a start failure, block-card replies fall back to static cards if independent block delivery was not actually sent, and late partial snapshots cannot append after a final has been committed.

## User Impact

Feishu replies that combine a text body with an image attachment now preserve both parts of the answer. If streaming close, streaming block delivery, or streaming-card startup fails, OpenClaw keeps or re-enters the final reply path instead of silently deduping the answer away and showing the no-visible-reply fallback.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-pipeline.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` (core 350 tests, Feishu 90 tests)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` (Feishu 90 tests)
- `git diff --check`
- Local Feishu proof image exists and parses as a valid PNG. A live retry before `ed94079`/`8a22d60` still returned the no-visible fallback; logs showed the model produced the expected text+`MEDIA:` final, then Feishu streaming startup failed with `Create card request failed with HTTP 400`, and no final was queued. Commits `ed94079` and `8a22d60` add streaming-start-failure and block-card-fallback coverage for that live gap.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` is clean after `8a22d60`: no accepted/actionable findings reported.

target.title: fix(scripts): report startup help stream errors when pipes fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers generating CLI startup metadata could lose a clear command-help rendering failure when the spawned help process stdout or stderr pipe emits a read error.

## Why This Change Was Made

`spawnText` now treats stdout and stderr read errors as first-class render errors, routes them through the existing child stop path, and reports the affected stream once the child closes. The change stays inside the startup metadata helper and covers both sibling output streams without changing CLI metadata shape or command selection.

## User Impact

Developers and release automation get an actionable startup metadata generation error instead of an unhandled pipe error or ambiguous child-process termination.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `spawnText` handles both stdout and stderr stream errors while preserving the existing command output cap and timeout coverage.
- Current-head focused proof at `9d2eab8fed0e8b7521345272003bcd38405b54da`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.test.ts` passed.
- Current-head real behavior proof at `9d2eab8fed0e8b7521345272003bcd38405b54da`: `node --import tsx <runtime proof script>` imported `scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.ts`, called `__testing.spawnText`, used real `node:child_process.spawn`, and triggered real child stdout/stderr pipe read errors from the parent process.

```text
stdout: runtime stdout render failed: stdout read error: stdout pipe failed from runtime proof

target.body:
Closes #101967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running CLI-backend sessions (e.g., `claude-cli`) with OAuth-only xAI auth would never see the `x_search` and `code_execution` tools on the session tool surface. Because subagents inherit the parent session's tool list, the tools were also stripped from native-runtime Grok subagents spawned from a claude-cli main session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway loopback MCP bridge that feeds CLI-backend sessions resolved plugin tools without passing an `authProfileStore`. Native embedded runs already passed the store, which let the xAI plugin register search/code-execution tools when an OAuth profile was present. This change threads the auth profile store through the same path and ensures the loopback surface uses the agent-local store without silently falling back to main credentials:

- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts and forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools`.
- `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` / `McpLoopbackToolCache` accept `authProfileStore` and `agentDir`; the cache key includes `agentDir` so different agents do not share tool entries.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` forwards its already-loaded `authStore` and resolved `agentDir` when computing prompt tools.
- The MCP loopback HTTP server resolves the per-session agent directory, loads the agent-local auth profile store, and passes both into tool resolution.
- `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime` gains an `excludeMainOverlay` option; the loopback path uses it so an expired or missing agent-local OAuth profile does not silently inherit the main store's OAuth identity.

## User Impact

CLI-backend sessions with OAuth-only xAI auth now correctly surface `x_search` and `code_execution`, and subagents spawned from those sessions inherit the tools as expected. Agent-local OAuth credentials stay scoped to the agent on the loopback surface.

## Evidence

- New focused tests:
  - `src/gateway/tool-resolution.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools` on both loopback and HTTP surfaces.
  - `src/gateway/mcp-http.runtime.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `resolveGatewayScopedTools`.
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` verifies `prepareCliRunContext` passes the loaded auth store and `agentDir` to loopback tool resolution.
  - `src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts` verifies `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime(agentDir, { excludeMainOverlay: true })` does not inherit main OAuth profiles.

target.title: fix(channel): bump wecom plugin pin to 2026.7.2 to fix concurrent-message session stuck (#102401)
target.body:
Closes #102401

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WeCom channel users sending multiple consecutive messages to an agent while one instruction is still processing would cause the session to get stuck permanently, requiring a restart to recover. All subsequent messages to that session are never processed after the stuck state is entered.

This is a regression: the behavior worked correctly before the 2026.5.x release cycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause lives in the external WeCom plugin package `@wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin`, not in OpenClaw core. The pinned version `2026.5.7` has a critical concurrency gap in its message handler (`monitor.js`): per-chat serialization via `enqueueWeComChatTask` was commented out, and incoming messages were directly dispatched via `await processWeComMessageNow(entry)`. When two messages from the same chat arrived concurrently, they bypassed OpenClaw's per-session `ReplyRunRegistry` guard and triggered `ForegroundReplyFence` suppression, leaving the earlier message's streaming reply stuck at `finish=false` and permanently blocking the session.

The upstream WeCom plugin team fixed this in `2026.7.2` by restoring the `enqueueWeComChatTask` serialization, which queues messages per `accountId:chatId` so each chat processes messages one at a time.

This PR is a narrow catalog pin update — no OpenClaw core changes are needed. The fix scope is limited to bumping the version and integrity hash in the official external channel catalog, along with updating the corresponding test assertions.

Non-goals:
- No changes to OpenClaw core queueing or session management (the correct fix layer is the external plugin)
- No behavioral changes for other channels or non-WeCom users

## User Impact

WeCom users no longer experience stuck sessions when sending rapid consecutive messages. Each message is processed sequentially per chat, and earlier streaming replies complete normally before the next message in the queue begins processing. Existing managed npm installs are automatically updated when users trigger plugin install or doctor flows with the updated catalog entry.

## Evidence

**Root cause verified by package diff** between `@wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin@2026.5.7` and `@wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin@2026.7.2`:

```
--- 2026.5.7  monitor.js  838-848
+++ 2026.7.2  monitor.js  846-856
-                // Queue logic temporarily disabled, process directly
-                // const { status } = enqueueWeComChatTask({...});
-                await processWeComMessageNow(entry);
+                // Serialize per accountId:chatId to ensure sequential processing,
+                // preventing concurrent ForegroundReplyFence suppression that
+                // leaves earlier streaming replies stuck at finish=false.
+                const { status } = enqueueWeComChatTask({
+                    accountId: entry.account.accountId,
+                    chatId: entry.chatId,
+                    task: () => processWeComMessageNow(entry),
+                });
+                if (status === "queued") {
+                    runtime.log?.(`[wecom] Chat task queued for chat=${entry.chatId} (previous task still running)`);
+                }
```

**Integrity hash verified** by downloading the tarball from npm registry and computing sha-512:

```bash
$ npm view @wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin@2026.7.2 dist.integrity
sha512-7kqdBIOF3SgDDoBoFtO6jxnxofbYSgbKdxZDNabD0y0jg2xKcVqlXZOOJ9+XQho/QOtIFrnRH2IRnPukFEYwJg==
```

**Test results** — all three affected test suites pass:

- `src/channels/plugins/catalog.test.ts`: **2 tests passed** ✓
- `src/channels/plugins/contracts/channel-catalog.contract.test.ts`: **12 tests passed** ✓
- `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`: **53 tests passed** ✓

**Build verification** — the official channel catalog is correctly generated with the updated pin:

```bash
$ node scripts/write-official-channel-catalog.mjs
npmSpec: @wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin@2026.7.2
integrity: sha512-7kqdBIOF3SgDDoBoFtO6jxnxofbYSgbKdxZDNabD0y0jg2xKcVqlXZOOJ9+XQho/QOtIFrnRH2IRnPukFEYwJg==
```

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw had no built-in isolated rescue watchdog that could detect an unhealthy managed gateway profile and repair it without going through the failing primary session.
- Why it matters: the larger rescue-watchdog feature is hard to review as one PR; this split lands the core runtime/service layer first so maintainers can review the actual watchdog mechanism without onboarding/UI noise.
- What changed: adds daemon/service hardening needed by the watchdog, introduces a new isolated `rescueWatchdog` cron payload + runner, and wires the gateway cron service to execute that watchdog job against a monitored profile.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no onboarding wizard flow, no CLI `openclaw onboard --rescue-watchdog` UX, and no docs changes in this PR.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #31480
- Supersedes #44113
- Supersedes #46493
- Supersedes #46499

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Adds a new internal isolated cron payload kind, `rescueWatchdog`, for watchdog jobs that monitor a target profile and repair it when unhealthy.
- Hardens LaunchAgent plist writes: trusted-home resolution, symlink rejection, atomic writes, and `0600` plist permissions.
- Managed service restart helpers now accept `AbortSignal`, so watchdog restart attempts can be canceled cleanly instead of hanging until command timeouts.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  The new capability is intentionally narrow: an isolated cron job can probe and repair a monitored local profile. Risk is bounded by restricting the payload shape, disallowing delivery targets for `rescueWatchdog`, resolving the monitored profile explicitly, and hardening the underlying managed-service restart and launchd plist write paths. The repair fallback uses exact argv via `process.execPath` and avoids shell-based PATH resolution.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / pnpm workspace
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): local managed gateway service / cron service only

### Steps

3. Build the repo and validate config to confirm the combined core layer compiles and loads cleanly.

### Expected

- Managed service restart helpers are abortable and launchd plist writes fail closed on unsafe targets.

### Actual

- Verified scenarios:
  - launchd plist path resolution ignores a conflicting `HOME` override, rejects symlink targets, and writes plist files with `0600` permissions via temp-file + rename.
  - `AbortSignal` now propagates through launchd/systemd/schtasks restart helpers into the process exec layer.
  - `rescueWatchdog` cron payloads normalize correctly, are forced to isolated session targets, and reject delivery/failureDestination config.
  - the rescue watchdog runner probes the monitored profile, attempts managed service restart, falls back to `doctor --repair --non-interactive`, and reports success/error summaries correctly.
- Edge cases checked:
  - `os.userInfo()` failure falls back to `os.homedir()`, and unresolved trusted home fails closed.
  - monitored rescue-profile names are rejected.
  - restart/repair flows respect cron timeout budget and abort behavior.
  - `launchd` temp plist files are cleaned up if rename fails.
- What you did **not** verify:

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this PR.
- Files/config to restore: `src/daemon/*`, `src/process/exec.ts`, `src/cron/*`, `src/rescue/watchdog-shared.ts`, `src/gateway/server-cron.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: launchd install unexpectedly failing on valid paths, or isolated cron jobs rejecting valid `agentTurn` jobs after the new payload kind was added.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: LaunchAgent path hardening could reject previously tolerated but unsafe filesystem layouts.
  - Mitigation: the checks are limited to symlinked/non-directory targets in the LaunchAgents path and have focused test coverage.
- Risk: adding a new cron payload kind could accidentally loosen validation or delivery behavior.
  - Mitigation: `rescueWatchdog` is explicitly restricted to isolated jobs, delivery is rejected, and schema/service/normalization paths have dedicated tests.
- Risk: watchdog repair code could leave stuck restart attempts behind.
  - Mitigation: abort propagation is threaded through the restart backends and the watchdog enforces bounded restart/repair timeouts.

Closes #100294

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound or outbound voice calls in conversation mode would crash the answered-call handler with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'enabled')` when the voice-call plugin was configured without a `realtime` object. The crash leaves the call hanging in an answered state with no initial greeting and no listening start.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/voice-call/src/manager.ts:416` read `this.config.realtime.enabled` without optional chaining. Every other reference in the voice-call codebase already uses `config.realtime?.enabled`. The change adds the missing optional-chain guard so an absent `realtime` section is treated as disabled, and the manager proceeds to speak the initial message and start listening as expected. A focused regression test constructs a `CallManager` with `realtime` removed and asserts that answering a conversation call still plays the greeting.

## User Impact

Voice-call setups that do not enable realtime voice-to-voice mode no longer crash on answer; the initial greeting and listening flow start normally.

I ran a standalone runtime script that uses the production `CallManager` + `MockProvider`, constructs a config with `realtime` removed, initiates a conversation call, and fires a `call.answered` event.

target.title: fix(trajectory): make window line sort comparator total-order safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`compareTrajectoryWindowLines` (`src/trajectory/runtime.ts`) sorted the trajectory window with subtraction:

```ts
const byTs = leftEvent.ts - rightEvent.ts;
if (byTs !== 0) return byTs;
return leftEvent.seq - rightEvent.seq;
```

`parseTrajectoryWindowLine` returns `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` for corrupted or unparseable JSONL lines (concurrent-write truncation, manual edits, foreign content appended to the file). **`Infinity - Infinity === NaN`**, so whenever two such lines are compared the comparator returns `NaN`. A comparator returning `NaN` violates `Array.sort`'s total-order contract (ES spec), producing engine-dependent, non-deterministic ordering of the trajectory window — even though the `Infinity` sentinel was clearly intended to sort bad lines last consistently.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** Subtraction is the wrong combinator when operands can be `Infinity`; `Infinity - Infinity` is `NaN`, not `0`.
- **Fix:** Compare with relational operators (`<`/`>`). Bad lines still sort last (`Infinity` compares greater than every finite `ts`), timestamp ties fall through to `seq`, and fully-equal lines get a deterministic raw-string tiebreak. The comparator now always returns a finite number in `{-1, 0, 1}`.
- This is the same lesson the sibling sort in `src/agents/tool-search.ts` already follows (it avoids `Infinity` subtraction and provides a total-order tiebreaker).

## User Impact

Trajectory window maintenance (`replaceTrajectoryWindow`) gets a deterministic sort even when the JSONL file contains corrupted lines — a real production state from truncated concurrent writes. No behavior change for well-formed files (finite timestamps sort identically). The corrupted lines are still retained, just consistently ordered at the tail.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

Reproduced with a `node` runtime script that compares the old subtraction comparator against the fixed relational comparator on a mixed set of valid + corrupted JSONL lines.

Terminal output of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-trajectory-sort.mjs` before/after the fix:

```
[BEFORE] oldCompare(two corrupt) = NaN (isNaN=true)
[PASS] old comparator returns NaN (reproduces bug)
[AFTER]  compareTrajectoryWindowLines(two corrupt) = -1
[PASS] fixed comparator returns a finite number, not NaN
[PASS] comparator is antisymmetric and never NaN on mixed set
[PASS] earliest good line sorts first
[PASS] corrupted lines sort last
```

The old comparator returns `NaN` (`Infinity - Infinity`) when comparing two corrupted lines, violating `Array.sort`'s total-order contract; the fixed comparator always returns a finite number, is antisymmetric, and sorts corrupted lines last.

## Real behavior proof

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | `compareTrajectoryWindowLines` returns `NaN` when comparing two corrupted/unparseable lines (`Infinity - Infinity`), violating `Array.sort`'s total-order contract. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `7fbb137b8f71a9a100e0319e7cdd66197ee030ac` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-trajectory-sort.mjs` — compares the old subtraction comparator against the fixed relational comparator on a mixed set of valid + corrupted lines; checks the result is never `NaN`, is antisymmetric, and sorts corrupted lines last. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):
```
[BEFORE] oldCompare(two corrupt) = NaN (isNaN=true)
[PASS] old comparator returns NaN (reproduces bug)
[AFTER]  compareTrajectoryWindowLines(two corrupt) = -1
[PASS] fixed comparator returns a finite number, not NaN
[PASS] comparator is antisymmetric and never NaN on mixed set
[PASS] earliest good line sorts first
[PASS] corrupted lines sort last
``` |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | The fixed comparator returns a finite number for every pair (including two corrupted lines, where the old path returned `NaN`); it is antisymmetric across the mixed set, orders valid lines by timestamp ascending, and places corrupted lines at the tail deterministically. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Determinism across multiple JS engines (only Node/V8 exercised here); the colocated unit test asserts the total-order invariant directly. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/trajectory/runtime.test.ts
✓ src/trajectory/runtime.test.ts (21 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  21 passed (21)
```

New tests cover: comparator never returns `NaN` for two corrupted lines, corrupted lines sort after valid ones, valid lines ordered by timestamp ascending, antisymmetry across a mixed set, and a deterministic sort with corrupted lines last. `compareTrajectoryWindowLines` is exported for direct testing.

target.title: fix(subagents): recover stalled child runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawned subagents can currently stall indefinitely without a structured recovery path. When a child run stops making progress, the parent session may never receive a useful completion/error result, leaving the task wedged until manual intervention. Issue #39305 asks for an escalating recovery path: nudge the stalled child first, then kill it and report the failure if it remains inactive.

Refs #39305

## Solution

- Add opt-in subagent stall recovery thresholds under `agents.defaults.subagents`.
- Freeze the stall policy on each registered run so later config changes do not alter in-flight recovery behavior.
- Nudge live child runs once after configured inactivity.
- Kill and report stalled runs after the configured timeout so the parent receives a terminal error instead of waiting forever.
- Wire the same policy through native subagent spawning and ACP `sessions_spawn` registry paths.
- Document the new config and add regression tests for nudge, kill, and policy resolution.

target.title: fix(matrix): truncate inbound preview on UTF-16 code-point boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Matrix inbound message handler builds a verbose log preview with `bodyText.slice(0, 200)`. When an inbound message contains a supplementary-plane character (emoji, extended CJK, etc.) whose surrogate pair straddles the 200th UTF-16 code unit, the slice splits the pair and emits a **lone surrogate** into the verbose log line. Lone surrogates corrupt JSON log serialization, break terminal rendering, and can crash UTF-8-validating log shippers.

This is the same defect class that #101630 just fixed for the Mattermost sibling monitor (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts:1681`); the Matrix monitor has the identical pre-fix line.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` operates on UTF-16 code units, so it can cut between the high and low surrogate of an astral character.
- **Fix:** Use the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (re-exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, the exact path the Mattermost fix uses) which backtracks to keep complete surrogate pairs intact.
- The helper already exists and is the canonical pattern; this PR only migrates the one remaining Matrix inbound-preview call site.

## User Impact

Verbose Matrix inbound logs no longer contain malformed lone surrogates. ASCII-only previews are unchanged (still capped at 200 code units). No effect on message routing, delivery, or the agent turn — only the verbose diagnostic preview string.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Sibling fix: #101630.

## Evidence

Reproduced with a `node` runtime script that builds an inbound body whose 200th code unit is a surrogate high (`\uD83D` from 😀), then compares the old `slice(0,200)` path against `truncateUtf16Safe`.

Terminal output of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-matrix-preview.mjs` before/after the fix:

```
[BEFORE] wellFormed=false preview-end="xx\ud83d"
[AFTER]  wellFormed=true preview-end="xxx"
[PASS] old slice(0,200) splits surrogate pair (reproduces bug)
[PASS] truncateUtf16Safe keeps complete pair at boundary
[PASS] plain ASCII still truncates to 200 (got 200)
[PASS] short input unchanged
```

The old path emits a lone high surrogate into the verbose log line; the fixed path stays well-formed UTF-16. ASCII previews are byte-identical (200 code units); short input is unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | Matrix inbound verbose preview (`bodyText.slice(0, 200)`) splits a surrogate pair when an emoji straddles the 200-code-unit boundary, emitting a lone surrogate into the log line. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `9d2d398c811bf5d604476a906f6b5d9066a20a74` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-matrix-preview.mjs` — builds an inbound body whose 200th code unit is a high surrogate (😀 = `\uD83D\uDE00`) and compares the old `slice(0,200)` path against `truncateUtf16Safe(body, 200)`. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):\n```\n[BEFORE] wellFormed=false preview-end="xx\ud83d"\n[AFTER]  wellFormed=true preview-end="xxx"\n[PASS] old slice(0,200) splits surrogate pair (reproduces bug)\n[PASS] truncateUtf16Safe keeps complete pair at boundary\n[PASS] plain ASCII still truncates to 200 (got 200)\n[PASS] short input unchanged\n``` |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | The fixed preview is well-formed UTF-16 (no lone surrogate); the old path is provably malformed (`wellFormed=false`, ending in the lone high surrogate `\ud83d`). Plain ASCII still truncates to exactly 200 code units; short input is unchanged. |
| 6 | What was not tested | End-to-end live Matrix homeserver traffic (no credentialled homeserver in this environment); the colocated unit test covers the truncation invariant directly. |

## Tests and validation

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, group conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. Raw Signal `replyToId` message-action inputs are handled by Signal's own send-payload preparation hook, matching the provider-owned shape used by channels like Telegram instead of special-casing Signal in shared outbound normalization.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal message action: raw `replyToId` send arguments are converted into durable payload `replyToId` by `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts`; canonical `replyTo` still stays on the core path, and existing payload `replyToId` values are preserved.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound group messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded Signal-owned cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, falls back to memory when persistent state is unavailable, and is limited to group conversations because direct replies derive their quote author from the target.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors without persistent author lookup.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Raw Signal `replyToId` action inputs are prepared in the Signal plugin payload hook; shared outbound normalization has no net Signal-specific change.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and register both the skipped message timestamp and edited target timestamp for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Calendar v3 events.list request deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Meet calendar lookup waited indefinitely if Google Calendar accepted the connection but never returned response headers. This blocked CLI and gateway flows that resolve a Meet URL from the user's Calendar.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Calendar owner now supplies a fixed 30-second deadline to the existing SSRF-guarded fetch. The original optional `timeoutMs` plumbing through three function signatures was removed because no production caller needs a separate deadline and the plugin should have one canonical policy.

The original 190-line loopback harness was replaced with a compact production-signal regression: a mocked stalled fetch receives the real guard's `AbortSignal`, remains active through 29,999 ms, then aborts at 30,000 ms with the production `TimeoutError`.

## User Impact

Calendar-based Google Meet lookup now fails with a bounded timeout instead of hanging the command or gateway request forever. Successful requests and existing function signatures are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Google Calendar's current reference documents `GET https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/calendarId/events`: https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/v3/reference/events/list
- Live unauthenticated request to that production endpoint: HTTP 403 in 0.051 seconds, confirming endpoint/network routing without exposing credentials.
- Linux Testbox focused timeout regression: 1/1 passed.
- Linux Testbox full Google Meet suite: 16 files, 200 tests passed.
- Linux Testbox touched-surface `pnpm check:changed`: production/test types, lint, import cycles, and repository guards passed.
- Fresh structured autoreview after the final test fix: clean, no accepted or actionable findings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

### Known proof gap

No user Calendar credential was used and no live Calendar request was deliberately held open for 30 seconds. The timeout boundary is forced deterministically through the production guarded-fetch signal.

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated


### Current-head proof (SHA `368c1f48d14f8b1d0cf0378d227c9d8e639787af`)

Refreshed after the per-agent lookup fix. Redacted terminal transcript posted in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101248#issuecomment-4921711199):

- `routes parent-targeted completions to requester session without channel delivery` — `announceTarget:"parent"` wakes the parent session with `deliver:false`, no channel announce.
- `keeps direct external delivery for dormant completion requesters` / `does not raw-send channel completions` — default `channel` route unchanged.
- Routing + config suite: 348/348 pass at this SHA; `tsgo` core + core-test, import-cycles (0), and `oxlint` (0/0) all green.

target.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
target.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

- Automation main refresh (2026-07-08 JST / 2026-07-07 UTC): merged `openclaw/openclaw@623534400684eca7c451cf587189fae714f2abe2` into the PR branch. The merge conflicted in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts` and `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`; resolved by keeping main's pre-connect send-evidence cleanup and this PR's no-budget reconciliation-deferral path/tests.
- Follow-up main refresh in the same run: `origin/main` advanced again to `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; merged it with no conflicts and pushed final head `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`.
- GitHub pre-refresh state checked: PR was open/ready with head `1779a704bc1b3a9e7b57e994fea534fac68c2eec`, base `a7c4a0471d944e3c3bf2b3071a5b1b485548dc8d`, `mergeable=CONFLICTING` via GraphQL, and the local branch was 378 commits behind `origin/main`.
- GitHub post-refresh state checked: PR head is `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`, base is `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; GitHub CI is pending on the refreshed head and `reviewDecision` remains empty/null.
- Review threads checked with GraphQL: 4 total, 0 unresolved. Existing connector reviews are `COMMENTED` only and are not treated as approval.
- `gh pr checks 87552 --repo openclaw/openclaw --required --json name,state,bucket,link,workflow`
  - GitHub reported no required checks on the PR branch.
- Current-head refresh validation:
  - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts` was attempted locally after the conflicted merge, but the infra Vitest runner produced no test output for 150s and was interrupted; the narrower recovery-file run also produced no test output for 120s and was interrupted. This hang was root-caused and fixed in the follow-up below.
  - Functional PR diff remains scoped to 7 files: 2 source, 4 tests, 1 docs; 293 insertions / 36 deletions.

## Follow-up (2026-07-09): infra shard hang, replay-pacing skip, and summary counters

Fixed in `1ab8620ebfc43fef70dbf258e3888338bcd704ec` (`fix(outbound): skip replay pacing for unreconcilable deferrals`).

- Root cause of the CI/local hang: `recoverPendingDeliveries` awaited `recoveryReplayPacer.wait(deadline)` (a real `sleep`) *before* `drainQueuedEntry` for every eligible entry, including ambiguous rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter that only defer. Under the recovery test's fake timers (`delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts:574`, "rechecks deferred ambiguous entries after the backoff elapses"), the pacer's `lastReplayStartedAt` equalled the frozen clock, so `wait()` scheduled a `RECOVERY_REPLAY_SPACING_MS` `sleep` that was never advanced. That deadlocked the module-singleton pacer mutex (`waitQueue`), which then hung every later test that paced. The merge that surfaced it advanced `origin/main` to `7ff3f2dbf922`; the pacing feature landed on the branch across the same range.
- Fix: resolve reconciliation availability (cheap adapter/`reconcileUnknownSend` capability check) before the pacer in both `recoverPendingDeliveries` and `drainPendingDeliveries`. No-reconciler ambiguous rows now defer as a no-op — they no longer pay the 250ms send-replay spacing or eat the 60s `maxRecoveryMs` deadline (addresses the 2026-07-07 Codex review). Entries that actually reconcile or replay pace exactly as before.
- Reporting: the no-reconciler deferral now increments a distinct `deferredNoReconciler` summary counter and log clause instead of being reported as a delivery failure, so operator logs match the persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0` state.
- Validation (local, current head `1ab8620`):

Behavior addressed: ambiguous outbound delivery entries whose platform send may have started must not be blindly replayed, and must remain pending/recoverable without consuming retry budget when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with Node v22.22.3, rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw@c5d34c8376f8aa32744786cae0473c60e39ef444`.

```text

pending entries: 1
queue row: {"status":"pending","retry_count":0,"recovery_state":"unknown_after_send","last_error":"delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"}
```

Observed result: recovery refused blind replay, did not call the delivery function, kept exactly one pending queue entry, and persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, and `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`.

```text

proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":0,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0,"deferredNoReconciler":1}
```

This corrected behavior is asserted deterministically by `delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` (e.g. "keeps entries abandoned after platform send may have started pending without reconciliation" and the new "does not spend replay pacing on unavailable-reconciler deferrals" case). target.title: Add Even Hub glasses bootstrap identity
target.body:
Related: #98227

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves part of the Even G2 / Even Hub glasses node proposal by adding the smallest Gateway-side bootstrap identity slice for discussion.

Even G2 is a product name, so this PR keeps the runtime/platform metadata broader: `platform: "even-hub"`, `deviceFamily: "glasses"`, and `modelIdentifier: "Even G2"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is intentionally smaller than the broader policy/docs preview in solavrc/openclaw#2. It does not import the Even Hub app, change node command policy defaults, enable Canvas plugin defaults, or add platform docs.

The shipped shape only:

- accepts `openclaw-even-g2-node` as a Gateway client id;
- allows matching Even Hub glasses metadata to use the existing native setup-code bootstrap path;
- keeps spoofed/mismatched metadata on the owner-approval path;
- keeps native/browser UI origin checks applied to the UI role;
- updates the plugin SDK API baseline for the exported client id surface.

## User Impact

No behavior changes for existing users unless a client connects with the new Even Hub glasses client id and matching metadata.

For Even G2 node development, this provides a concrete minimal seam for maintainer review before any app import, node command policy defaults, Canvas defaults, or docs are proposed.

## Evidence

Local validation:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts src/gateway/server.ios-client-id.test.ts
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check
```

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped prepare the patch and run validation.


## Real behavior proof (2026-07-03)

Live, out-of-process proof against a gateway started from this branch
(`node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev gateway`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`,
token auth). Setup codes were issued with the real CLI (`openclaw qr --json`) and a
standalone WebSocket client performed the full v3 device-auth connect handshake
(`connect.challenge` nonce, signed payload, `auth.bootstrapToken`). The client connected
with remote locality (`x-forwarded-for`), so silent local pairing cannot explain the results.

**Case A — genuine Even Hub glasses metadata → silent bootstrap approval.**
Client `{"id":"openclaw-even-g2-node","platform":"even-hub","mode":"node","deviceFamily":"glasses","modelIdentifier":"Even G2"}`:

```jsonc

{

  "payload": {
    "type": "hello-ok",
    "auth": {
      "role": "node",
      "scopes": [],
      "deviceToken": "[redacted]",
      "deviceTokens": [
        {
          "deviceToken": "[redacted]",
          "role": "operator",
          "scopes": ["operator.approvals", "operator.read", "operator.talk.secrets", "operator.write"]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Presence snapshot after connect shows the paired node:
`Node: openclaw-even-g2-node · platform even-hub · deviceFamily glasses · modelIdentifier Even G2 · mode node`.

**Case B — same client id, spoofed `deviceFamily: "watch"` → owner approval required.**

```jsonc

  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "NOT_PAIRED",
    "message": "pairing required: device is not approved yet",
    "details": { "code": "PAIRING_REQUIRED", "reason": "not-paired", "requestId": "2469936f-…" }
  }
}
```

**Case C — `node-host` client id with glasses metadata → owner approval required.**
Same `NOT_PAIRED` / `PAIRING_REQUIRED` shape (requestId `57362fb0-…`).

**CLI state after the three connects** (`openclaw devices list`, same isolated gateway):

```text
Pending (2)

  2469936f-… device 4111ed90…  roles: node; scopes: none   new pairing   ← Case B
Paired
  f8ba40a3…  roles node, operator

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts src/gateway/server.ios-client-id.test.ts  # 43 passed

`openclaw-even-g2-node` is the shipping external app's current id, but it bakes one hardware

target.title: fix(plugins): fall back to os.homedir() when HOME/OPENCLAW_HOME is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/plugins/manifest-metadata-scan.ts` resolved the home directory with:

```ts
const home = env.OPENCLAW_HOME ?? env.HOME ?? env.USERPROFILE ?? os.homedir();
return path.join(home, ".openclaw");
```

The nullish coalescing operator (`??`) only catches `null`/`undefined`. An **empty or whitespace** home variable — e.g. `HOME=""`` in a stripped-down container, sandbox, or cron env that clears `HOME` — is *not* nullish, so it is kept as `""`. Then `path.join("", ".openclaw")` yields the **relative** path `".openclaw"` under the current working directory instead of falling through to `os.homedir()`. The same flaw affects the `~`-expansion branch in `resolveUserPath`.

Result: plugin discovery reads global extensions from the wrong directory (cwd-relative `.openclaw/extensions` instead of the real home).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** `??` is nullish-only; an empty string is a valid, non-nullish value that bypasses the fallback chain.
- **Fix:** Normalize each candidate with the already-imported `normalizeOptionalString` (aliased as `normalizeTrimmedString` in this file), which returns `undefined` for empty/whitespace strings. An empty value then falls through to `os.homedir()`, matching the canonical home resolver in `src/infra/home-dir.ts` (whose `normalize()` helper explicitly returns `undefined` for empty/whitespace/"`undefined`"/"`null`" strings).
- The helper was already imported and used for `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; this extends the same normalization to the home-resolution chain.

## User Impact

In environments where `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_HOME` is set but empty, plugin manifest scanning now correctly resolves the state directory under the real OS home. Valid (non-empty) home values are unchanged. No effect when home variables are unset (already fell back to `os.homedir()`).

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

Reproduced with a `node` runtime script comparing the fixed `normalizeOptionalString`-based home chain against the old `??` chain for empty/whitespace/set/unset HOME values.

Terminal output of `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-manifest-home.mjs`:

```
os.homedir() = "/home/0668000781"
[PASS] HOME empty string: fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was ".openclaw", CHANGED)
[PASS] OPENCLAW_HOME empty string: fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was ".openclaw", CHANGED)
[PASS] HOME whitespace: fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was "   /.openclaw", CHANGED)
[PASS] HOME set (regression): fixed="/home/test/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was "/home/test/.openclaw", same)
[PASS] no env (fallback to os.homedir): fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was "/home/0668000781/.openclaw", same)
```

Empty/whitespace HOME now resolves to an absolute path under `os.homedir()`; valid HOME and unset-HOME cases are unchanged (no regression).

## Real behavior proof

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | `HOME=""` (or whitespace) made `resolveStateDir` return a relative `.openclaw` instead of falling back to `os.homedir()`, because `??` does not treat empty string as nullish. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `6875e6a39dadb45e98fd322934fb836bc4573b70` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-manifest-home.mjs` — compares the fixed `normalizeOptionalString`-based chain against the old `??` chain for empty/whitespace/set/unset HOME cases. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):
```
os.homedir() = "/home/0668000781"
[PASS] HOME empty string: fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was ".openclaw", CHANGED)
[PASS] OPENCLAW_HOME empty string: fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was ".openclaw", CHANGED)
[PASS] HOME whitespace: fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was "   /.openclaw", CHANGED)
[PASS] HOME set (regression): fixed="/home/test/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was "/home/test/.openclaw", same)
[PASS] no env (fallback to os.homedir): fixed="/home/0668000781/.openclaw" isAbsolute=true (old was "/home/0668000781/.openclaw", same)
``` |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | Empty/whitespace HOME now resolves to an absolute path under `os.homedir()`; valid HOME and unset-HOME cases are byte-identical to the old behavior (no regression). |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live plugin discovery on a container with a cleared HOME env (the colocated unit test covers the resolver directly across empty/whitespace/set/override cases). |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/manifest-metadata-scan.test.ts
✓ src/plugins/manifest-metadata-scan.test.ts (6 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  6 passed (6)
```

New tests assert: empty HOME → absolute path under `os.homedir()`; whitespace `OPENCLAW_HOME` → same fallback; valid HOME unchanged (regression); `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` override still honored with empty HOME. `resolveStateDir` is exported for direct testing (the module-level scan cache makes end-to-end assertion impractical).

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only the home-resolution fallback in `manifest-metadata-scan.ts`.
- [x] No config/env/default surface change (no new env var; existing vars handled more robustly).
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change.
- [x] Backward compatible — valid home values produce identical results; only empty/whitespace values now correctly fall back.
- [x] No new deps (reuses the already-imported `normalizeOptionalString`).
- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

- [x] Allow edits by maintainers
