target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```

target.title: fix(backup): write backup archive with owner-only 0o600 permissions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup` writes its `.tar.gz` archive world-readable (0644), so any other local user can read every credential out of the published backup. The archive bundles `auth.json` (OAuth access and refresh tokens), `openclaw.json` (provider API keys), and the state database, all in one file that lands group- and world-readable.

The intermediate SQLite snapshot inside the flow is already hardened to `0o600` (`src/infra/backup-create.ts:732`), so the module already treats these bytes as secret, but that mitigation never reached the final archive that actually leaves the machine.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause is `src/infra/backup-create.ts:194`. The single shared archive writer creates the output stream with no `mode`, so the file is created 0644 (minus umask):

```ts
// before
await pipeline(params.archiveStream, createWriteStream(params.archivePath));
```

`publishTempArchive` then hard-links (`fs.link`, :357) or copies (`fs.copyFile`, :371) that temp file to the final output path, and both carry the 0644 mode through to the published artifact.

The fix creates the stream owner-only from the start:

```ts
// after
await pipeline(params.archiveStream, createWriteStream(params.archivePath, { mode: 0o600 }));
```

`createWriteStream` opens the file with `O_CREAT` and this mode, so there is no world-readable window. `writeArchiveStreamToFile` is the one funnel every archive write (initial attempt and every `.retry-N` retry) passes through before publish, so hardening it once covers all callers. `fs.link` shares the inode (same mode) and `fs.copyFile` copies the source mode, so the single write-site change reaches both publish paths without touching `publishTempArchive`. This mirrors the existing `0o600` chmod already applied to the SQLite snapshot in the same module. Only the file mode changes; archive contents, layout, and verification are untouched.

## User Impact

Backups created by `openclaw backup` are now owner-only (`-rw-------`). Operators on shared or multi-user hosts no longer leak OAuth tokens, provider API keys, and state to other local accounts through a world-readable backup file. Existing archives are unaffected; the new mode applies to newly created backups.

## Evidence

Drove the real `createBackupArchive` production entry point on a real on-disk OpenClaw state tree seeded with a provider API key in `openclaw.json`, on pristine `origin/main` 735dbd2 and on the patched tree, then `ls -l` on the produced archive and extracted its bytes with `tar -xzO | grep`. State discovery, the tar archiver, and the publish path all stayed real; nothing was faked.

Steps: seed `openclaw.json` with `sk-PROOF-SECRET-TOKEN-0123456789`, run `createBackupArchive({ output, includeWorkspace: false })`, then `ls -l <archive>` and `tar -xzOf <archive> | grep -c <secret>`.

```
# BEFORE (pristine main 735dbd2)
ls -l archive: -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 20919 Jul  9 03:46 .../backups/2026-05-09T12-00-00.000+00-00-openclaw-backup.tar.gz
archived files containing the raw API key: 1
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
ls -l archive: -rw------- 1 root root 20918 Jul  9 03:46 .../backups/2026-05-09T12-00-00.000+00-00-openclaw-backup.tar.gz
archived files containing the raw API key: 1
```

Before the change the produced archive is `-rw-r--r--` (readable by every local user) while carrying the raw API key inside it; after the change the same archive is `-rw-------`, owner-only, so the credential is no longer exposed to other local users.

Regression and checks:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-create.test.ts`: 42 passed, including the new `writes the published archive with owner-only 0o600 permissions`.
- The new test fails on pristine `origin/main` (`expected 420 to be 384`, i.e. 0o644 vs 0o600) and passes with the patch.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` / `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` are clean on the changed files.

Not covered: no live provider request and no full build were run; the `fs.copyFile` publish fallback (only reached when the target filesystem rejects hard links) was not driven end to end, though it provably preserves the source `0o600` mode.

## Summary

Draft review PR for the CLI catalog effort described in the RFC: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/rfcs/blob/codex/cli-catalog-overlay-rfc/rfcs/0010-cli-catalog-overlay.md

This adds a read-only catalog view over existing OpenClaw command/tool surfaces rather than a second command system. It covers:

- `openclaw catalog list` JSON/Markdown output
- runtime command, plugin descriptor, and supplied node/operator command lenses
- prompt projection from catalog metadata, including a scoped `node-operator` prompt view
- audit, test-matrix, and operator summary views
- schema fixtures, generated docs, and advisory report artifacts
- plugin descriptor catalog metadata preservation through registry normalization

The goal is to make commands, routed operations, plugin commands, node/operator commands, prompt-visible surfaces, audit views, and operator/test planning easier to inspect and discuss from one place.

## Scout / node-mode evidence

Node/operator support is now folded through the six-PR stack instead of being staged as a separate follow-up. The live motivation is the node-mode work in `gim-home/m`:

- `gim-home/m#4045`: node-routed MCP commands such as `mcp.help`, `mcp.invoke`, `mcp.status`, and `mcp.cancel`
- `gim-home/m#4086`: filesystem node commands such as `filesystem.read`, `filesystem.write`, and `filesystem.patch`
- `gim-home/m#4088`: browser/file-open node commands such as `browser.open` and `file.openWithDefaultApp`

That stack shows why the catalog needs scoped lenses, not just broad inventory. A node-operating agent needs a small prompt view of available node commands, argument hints, risk, confirmation, and approval boundaries that match the actual Desktop/Gateway implementation.

## Proposed stack

This draft PR contains the six catalog slices folded together for directional review:

1. Foundation catalog view, including the supplied `cli.nodeCommands` contract
2. Dynamic inventory and operator lenses, including node command audit/test/summary fields
3. Prompt projection, including the scoped `node-operator` prompt view
4. Schema fixtures for list/audit/test-matrix/summary/prompt contracts
5. Generated reference docs
6. Hardening, advisory reports, plugin metadata preservation, and consumer boundary

The same stack is also pushed as reviewable branch heads on the fork:

- PR1: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/tree/user/giodl/cli-catalog-review-foundation
- PR2: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/tree/user/giodl/cli-catalog-review-dynamic-lenses

- PR6: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/tree/user/giodl/cli-catalog-review-hardening

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli-catalog-overlay/list.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/prompt-projection.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/audit.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/test-matrix.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/operator-summary.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/schema-fixtures.test.ts src/cli-catalog-overlay/consumer-contract.test.ts test/scripts/generate-cli-catalog-doc.test.ts test/scripts/cli-catalog-overlay-report.test.ts --reporter=dot`

target.title: feat(session-message-events) socket.drain
target.body:
## Summary

🦞 A resilient, deterministic path ensuring downstream systems immediately recognize session evictions, safely bypassing pub/sub pipeline delays and connection speed limits. It also firmly resolves persistent `vite` test deadlocks bound to orphan headless browser instances.
- **Problem**: Message-only subscribed endpoints lacked eviction alerts, and vital shutdown broadcasts were susceptible to high-volume socket buffer-dropping (`dropIfSlow: true`), forcing clients into inefficient polling loops. Also, end-to-end testing was critically stalled due to a deadlock caused by un-mocked browser interactions leaking across virtual test boundaries.
- **Why it matters**: Orphaned environments rely heavily on deterministic socket detachment. Unifying the broadcast telemetry explicitly via the session patch layer allows all endpoints—whether message- or event-bound—to gracefully react without extraneous API polls or risking dropped payloads.
- **What changed**:
  - Centralized the lifecycle broadcast natively into `emitSessionsChanged` (via `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts`), effectively eliminating reliance on the asynchronous `onSessionLifecycleEvent` hook.
  - Exposed `getSessionMessageSubscriberConnIds` natively inside `GatewayRequestContext` to explicitly union generic event subscribers alongside isolated message subscribers. 
  - Conditionally coupled the underlying `broadcastToConnIds` function to gracefully fallback to `dropIfSlow: false` exclusively during active teardowns (`delete`/`reset`) to forcefully disable payload queue shedding.
  - Registered `"socket.drain"` with `[READ_SCOPE]` in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS` (`src/gateway/server-broadcast.ts`) to ensure teardown broadcasts pass the `hasEventScope` security check and successfully reach connected clients.
  - Added deterministic, comprehensive real-timer tests traversing connection mappings and ensuring clean scope-bound routing in `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`.
  - Resolved `vitest` suite deadlocks by explicitly mocking `closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions` in `src/gateway/test-helpers.mocks.ts` to prevent HTTP request leaks against dead CDP instances.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**: No existing contracts or `socket.drain` payloads were modified in structure. This is 100% additive logic expanding target scope precision.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #63374


## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: 
  1. Added `socket.drain` lifecycle events to websocket `sessions.messages.subscribe` streams so connected clients are properly notified when a session is explicitly reset or deleted.
  2. Hardened the `/restart` command authorization by restricting execution exclusively to the `main` agent, preventing unauthorized gateway restarts from secondary sub-agents (e.g., `tg2`, `tg3`).
  3. Fixed test locking errors and scope issues (`operator.admin`) in the test harness.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS development environment running the OpenClaw gateway (`v2026.5.24`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
  Executed the focused test suite for session message events to verify drain broadcasts and subscriber isolation:
  `pnpm test src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 
  **Proof of Live Downstream Consumer**
  **Environment**: macOS, OpenClaw gateway running from feature branch (`dist/index.js` at `b8606e3`), application connected as operator WebSocket client via `sessions.subscribe`.
  **Before this patch**: Message-only subscribers (`sessions.messages.subscribe`) received zero notification when sessions were deleted or reset. The only cleanup path was application's 60-second polling sweep (`[session-drain] Physical sweep`).
  **After this patch**: The gateway emits `socket.drain` events on session lifecycle mutations. Application receives them in real-time and flushes immediately.
  **Steps**:
  1. Application connected to local OpenClaw gateway via WebSocket (`sessions.subscribe`)
  2. Orchestration tasks spawned agent sessions (`manager`, `evolver`)
  3. Sessions were deleted during normal lifecycle cleanup
  4. Application received `socket.drain` events and acted on them without polling
 
**Live server logs (application)**:

```
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307 
[session-drain] Database sweep: removed 3 tracked orphaned session(s) 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307
```

**What this proves**: Three sessions were evicted via `socket.drain` → Application flushed each from SQLite immediately (the `[CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction` log). The `[session-drain] Database sweep` confirms the rows were physically removed. Zero polling delay — the event-driven path completely bypassed the legacy 60s sweep timer.
- **Observed result after fix**: All `16` tests passed successfully. The test suite confirms that `socket.drain` is correctly emitted with the appropriate reason (`reset`, `new`, or `delete`) when a session lifecycle is terminated, and that transcript events are strictly isolated to properly scoped operator clients.
- **What was not tested**: Frontend UI (React) receiving `socket.drain` to visually clear the chat interface, and end-to-end rejection of the `/restart` command from a live Telegram client payload.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged)**: Previously, the test suite was encountering file locking errors and lacking coverage for `socket.drain` broadcasts during session resets and deletions. Resolved.


## Root Cause

- **Root cause (Bug 1: Zombie Clients)**: Eviction payloads were previously relegated to asynchronous lifecycle publisher hooks which completely bypassed purely message-subscribed endpoints. Furthermore, even when `socket.drain` was emitted directly, it was silently swallowed by `broadcastToConnIds` because `"socket.drain"` lacked an entry in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS`, failing the gateway's `hasEventScope` security check. Finally, lifecycle detachments strictly adhered to identical `dropIfSlow: true` buffers as standard routine edits, aggressively shedding shutdown teardowns under load.
- **Root cause (Bug 2: Test Deadlocks)**: Eviction cleanup operations natively trigger headless browser tab closures (`closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions`). Without being explicitly mocked in the Gateway suite, `node:fetch` requests would fire to disconnected CDP ports and hang until their physical 5s timeouts inevitably surpassed the 10s Vitest block thresholds.
- **Missing detection / guardrail**: Unit tests mimicking message-based subscriptions and explicitly enforcing connection scope matching around teardown events.
- **Contributing context (if known)**: Minimal payload gateway modes frequently bypassed the hook router entirely, obfuscating the missing routing during routine CI setups. 

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level that should have caught this**:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file**: `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Scenario the test should lock in**: Validate that explicitly isolated `session.message` subscriptions successfully ingest `socket.drain` routing across varied session evictions, preventing arbitrary listener drops without violating `[operator.admin]` permission structures.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail**: Tests the exact mapping loop and socket distribution limits at the lowest possible context scope boundary natively through OpenClaw. 
- **Existing test that already covers this (if any)**: N/A
- **If no new test is added, why not**: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. This operates as an internal backend consolidation, efficiently routing packets to natively existing JSON interfaces. Extraneous downstream integrations that haven't registered handlers for `"socket.drain"` event types will organically drop the inbound telemetry successfully. 

## Diagram (if applicable)

N/A

## Security Impact (required)
- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Base Node
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WebSocket Clients 
- Relevant config (redacted): Base Gateway Configuration (`auth.mode = "none"/"token"`)

### Steps

1. Attach an operator to the target `sessions.messages.subscribe` endpoint. 
2. Actively execute `sessions.delete` or `sessions.reset` natively as an `operator.admin` against the tracked target.
3. Validate deterministic receipt of the `socket.drain` telemetry sequence via the local connection buffer. 

### Expected

- `socket.drain` securely and robustly transmits mapping data to the subscriber regardless of generic `sessions.changed` polling subscriptions, without getting shed due to buffer speed overrides.

### Actual

- The telemetry payload flows beautifully without throwing. 

## Evidence

Attach at least one:
- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Ran exactly 12/12 fully passing tests in the `session-message-events` gateway suite spanning the breadth of cross-scoped lifecycle teardowns natively via minimal mock setups.
- Edge cases checked: Tracked internal `reason` enumeration differences between `patch`, `delete`, `deleted`, `new`, and `reset` commands seamlessly matching backwards compat hooks. 
- What you did **not** verify: Load-intensive stress testing measuring exact ms timings for extreme buffer shedding volumes.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: Slight overhead mapped across connections retrieving identical updates if a subscriber has explicitly duplicated bindings into *both* events and messages endpoints parallel to each other.
  - **Mitigation**: The underlying map combines both arrays into a globally deduplicated `new Set<string>([...evSubs, ...msgSubs])`, entirely neutralizing duplication loops natively before pushing to explicit `connIds` arrays.

target.title: security: deny-all top-level token permissions on release workflows; maintainer-skill temp-file hygiene
target.body:
## Summary

Security hardening in three small pieces, all metadata/docs-only (no runtime code):

1. **Top-level `permissions: {}` on the 6 release workflows** (`docker-release`, `macos-release`, `openclaw-npm-release`, `openclaw-release-checks`, `plugin-clawhub-release`, `plugin-npm-release`). Audited every job in all six workflows: each already declares its own job-level `permissions`, so the implicitly permissive workflow-default `GITHUB_TOKEN` was unused attack surface. Deny-all at the top level makes the job-level declarations the single source of truth.
2. **GHSA maintainer skill — temp-file hygiene**: the documented pattern used fixed, predictable `/tmp/ghsa.*` paths for pre-publish advisory drafts (sensitive until published). Now uses `mktemp -d` + a cleanup `trap`. Also fixes the verify example, which read `/tmp/ghsa.refetch.json` without any step ever writing that file — it now captures the `gh api` refetch into a variable and checks `state`/`published_at`/escaped-newline in one pass. Follow-up (ClawSweeper P2 + two defects found while reproducing it): the escaped-newline check now gates explicitly with `if … rg -q …` printing `FAIL`/`PASS` instead of leaving the bare `rg` exit as the result (rg exits 0 exactly when the forbidden literal `\n` is present, so the bad state looked like the passing path); the pattern is now `rg '\\n'` (the previous `rg '\\\\n'` matched two backslashes + `n` and never matched the guarded sample); and the snippet uses `printf '%s'` instead of `echo` (zsh/dash `echo` rewrites backslash escapes, turning the JSON's escaped backslash-n into a real newline before jq/rg see it — hiding the very thing the check guards).
3. **Secret-scanning maintainer skill**: the Step 7 example used a fixed `/tmp/results.json`, contradicting the skill's own "mktemp with random UUIDs for all temp files" rule — now uses a `mktemp -d` work dir. The commit-leak section previously said only "Cannot clean. Notify author…"; it now includes context gathering (is the commit on an open PR?) and situation-matched remediation templates (amend for the latest commit, rebase for an older one, escalate-without-force-push-instructions when merged to the default branch).

Deliberately **not** included (evaluated and dropped):

- Wiring `lint:tmp:dynamic-import-warts` into the CI boundary checks: the script is advisory-by-default and the tree currently has 4 outstanding findings (matrix, qa-lab, qa-matrix, qqbot), so gating it is a separate ratcheting effort.
- Migrating `extensions/acpx/index.ts` to `definePluginEntry()`: 48 of 139 bundled entries still use the plain-object pattern, so a single-plugin migration is churn, not a completion.

## Verification

Metadata/docs-only change; validated with the light path:

- `git diff --check` — clean.
- YAML parse + semantic assert on all 6 workflows (`permissions` parses to `{}` at top level, `jobs` intact).
- Per-job permissions audit: every job in all 6 workflows declares job-level `permissions`, so deny-all cannot strip a permission any job relies on.
- `oxfmt --check` on all 8 changed files — clean (repo-wide `pnpm format:check` fails on 193 pre-existing files on current `main`, unrelated to this change).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Implicitly permissive workflow-default `GITHUB_TOKEN` on the 6 release workflows; predictable fixed `/tmp` temp paths plus a verify example that read a never-written file in the GHSA and secret-scanning maintainer skills.
Real environment tested: Local source checkout on top of `openclaw/openclaw@2ba622ca301` (macOS, Node 25, pnpm 11.2.2). The change is CI metadata + skill docs only; no app runtime surface exists to exercise.

target.title: fix(crestodian): run approval-intent classifier on the utilityModel, not flagship (#102360)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Crestodian approval-intent classifier (`classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent`, `src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts`) resolves the completion model **without** `useUtilityModel: true`, so an ambiguous approval reply that reaches the model path runs on the agent's **flagship** model to decide a single approve/decline/other label. It was the only member of the simple-completion family (e.g. `conversation-label-generator.ts`) that omitted the flag, so every ambiguous approval reply is billed at flagship pricing for a fixed ~8-token structured answer. Fixes #102360.

## Why This Change Was Made

A one-word bounded classification is exactly the "utility work" the rest of the family already runs on the configured `utilityModel`. `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` already supports `useUtilityModel` (resolves `agents.defaults.utilityModel`); the classifier just wasn't passing it. Adding `useUtilityModel: true` aligns it with the family and the cheaper tier.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a distinct `utilityModel` (the intended cheap tier for bounded classification) stop paying flagship pricing for ambiguous approval-flow replies. No behavior change to the classification result — only the model tier that judges it.

## Evidence

Real `classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent` call with an ambiguous message (model path), capturing what model prep receives:
```
before (main):    prepare called with useUtilityModel = undefined   ← flagship
after  (this PR): prepare called with useUtilityModel = true        ← utilityModel
```
Added a regression test asserting `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` is called with `{ useUtilityModel: true }`. `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `approval-intent.test.ts` green (8 tests: 7 existing + 1 new).

target.title: improve(android): manage configured model providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Android users could only see provider readiness summaries in Settings > Providers & Models, without a clear list of provider-configured model IDs or direct controls to verify, add, or remove provider model definitions.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a provider-model management path for the Android app. The screen now loads a provider-configured model view, expands each provider to show its model IDs, and exposes model availability checks plus add/remove controls.

The review surfaced a source-of-truth risk: the existing `models.list` configured view can be affected by `agents.defaults.models` allowlists, while add/remove operations write `models.providers.*.models`. This update fixes that by adding a source-aware `models.list` view, `provider-config`, and making Android management use that view. The normal picker-style `configured` view keeps its existing allowlist behavior.

Follow-up review also surfaced an Android code-quality issue: the shared Android `modelCatalog` state was being reused by both normal picker/health consumers and the Providers & Models management screen. This update splits the Android state so:

- `modelCatalog` remains the normal configured picker/catalog view.
- `providerModelCatalog` is dedicated to Settings > Providers & Models and uses `view: "provider-config"`.

That keeps the management source of truth aligned without changing unrelated Android model consumers.

Model configuration writes are handled by `models.configure` and `models.remove` gateway RPC methods that operate on `snapshot.sourceConfig`, not the runtime-expanded config. That keeps Android from accidentally persisting bundled/default runtime model catalog entries when adding or removing one model.

## User Impact

Android users can now:

- View provider-configured model providers and detailed model IDs under each provider.
- Refresh provider/model availability from Gateway.
- Check whether an individual model is currently available from the Gateway catalog/readiness view.
- Add or update a provider-configured model ID without editing config files manually.
- Remove an authored provider model with a confirmation dialog.

## Evidence

- Android UI/state tests in `ProviderModelStatusTest` for provider model rows, availability readiness, and model-test result keys.
- Gateway handler tests in `config.shared-auth.test.ts` proving `models.configure` and `models.remove` write only authored provider models and do not persist runtime-only default catalog entries.
- Gateway model-list tests proving `models.list` `provider-config` returns provider-authored rows even when `agents.defaults.models` allowlists exist, and does not show allowlist-only models.

target.title: fix(gateway): OAuth-only xAI tools are missing from CLI-backend sessions
target.body:
Closes #101967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running CLI-backend sessions (e.g., `claude-cli`) with OAuth-only xAI auth would never see the `x_search` and `code_execution` tools on the session tool surface. Because subagents inherit the parent session's tool list, the tools were also stripped from native-runtime Grok subagents spawned from a claude-cli main session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway loopback MCP bridge that feeds CLI-backend sessions resolved plugin tools without passing an `authProfileStore`. Native embedded runs already passed the store, which let the xAI plugin register search/code-execution tools when an OAuth profile was present. This change threads the auth profile store through the same path and ensures the loopback surface uses the agent-local store without silently falling back to main credentials:

- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts and forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools`.
- `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` / `McpLoopbackToolCache` accept `authProfileStore` and `agentDir`; the cache key includes `agentDir` so different agents do not share tool entries.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` forwards its already-loaded `authStore` and resolved `agentDir` when computing prompt tools.
- The MCP loopback HTTP server resolves the per-session agent directory, loads the agent-local auth profile store, and passes both into tool resolution.
- `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime` gains an `excludeMainOverlay` option; the loopback path uses it so an expired or missing agent-local OAuth profile does not silently inherit the main store's OAuth identity.

## User Impact

CLI-backend sessions with OAuth-only xAI auth now correctly surface `x_search` and `code_execution`, and subagents spawned from those sessions inherit the tools as expected. Agent-local OAuth credentials stay scoped to the agent on the loopback surface.

## Evidence

- New focused tests:
  - `src/gateway/tool-resolution.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools` on both loopback and HTTP surfaces.
  - `src/gateway/mcp-http.runtime.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `resolveGatewayScopedTools`.
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` verifies `prepareCliRunContext` passes the loaded auth store and `agentDir` to loopback tool resolution.
  - `src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts` verifies `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime(agentDir, { excludeMainOverlay: true })` does not inherit main OAuth profiles.
  - `extensions/xai/src/xai-oauth-tool-registration.test.ts` verifies the xAI plugin registers `x_search` and `code_execution` when an OAuth auth context is present.

- Existing suites still pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.cron-regression.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts`

## Real behavior proof

The following is a redacted runtime transcript produced by `scripts/proof/xai-oauth-loopback-tools.ts`. It exercises the actual changed gateway path:

1. Builds a real plugin registry and registers the bundled xAI plugin through a real `registerTool` handler (so `code_execution` and `x_search` are actually recorded in the registry).
2. Loads an OAuth-only xAI auth profile store (tokens redacted).
3. Calls `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ surface: "loopback", authProfileStore, agentDir })` — the same function used by the CLI-backend loopback/MCP tool surface.
4. Prints the resulting MCP `tools/list` JSON-RPC response.

All private tokens, account IDs, phone numbers, IPs, and non-public endpoints are redacted.

target.title: fix(feishu): preserve text when replies include media
target.body:
Closes #102390

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users would lose the visible text from an assistant final reply when that reply also included a regular `MEDIA:` attachment while streaming cards were active. The channel could finish with only the no-visible-content fallback instead of showing the assistant's text alongside the attachment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu streaming reply path now closes the active final streaming card before dispatching regular media attachments, and it falls back to a normal text send first if the streaming close reports that no text became visible. That keeps the final text visible while preserving the existing separate media send behavior and the voice-media text suppression path.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Feishu replies that combine text with an image or other regular attachment now keep the assistant's text visible and still send the attachment. Users should no longer see the misleading "reply completed without visible content" fallback for this text-plus-media streaming reply shape.

## Evidence

Source-level before/premise: on current main, the active streaming branch updated the final text and then returned after media dispatch without closing the streaming card in that branch. Feishu media sending does not carry a caption parameter, so the text needs to be made visible through the streaming card path, or sent as plain text when the card close reports that no text became visible.

After fix:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` -> 88 tests passed, including final text plus regular media and close-false fallback coverage.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` -> passed.

target.title: fix(process): add zombie reaper to prevent child process leak
target.body:
Closes #97616

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running openclaw gateway processes in Docker accumulate zombie processes over time. One user reported 800+ zombie processes (`openclaw-hooks`, `bash`, `codex`, `chrome-headless`) after running openclaw 2026.6.10 for several months. Each zombie consumes a PID slot and kernel resources. When the process limit is exhausted, the runtime degrades (`spawn EAGAIN`, `uv_thread_create`, gateway instability, connector silence).

**Root cause**: When openclaw kills a process tree via `kill(-pid, SIGKILL)`, grandchildren may exit and become zombies **before** their parent (openclaw's direct child) is killed. When the group leader dies, the zombie grandchildren are reparented to PID 1, but **no new SIGCHLD is sent** because the grandchildren already exited. The zombies remain permanently unreaped.

libuv already calls `waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)` in a loop inside its SIGCHLD handler, which would reap these zombies — but the SIGCHLD never fires for processes that exited before being reparented.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a lightweight zombie reaper (`src/process/zombie-reaper.ts`) with two mechanisms:

1. **Post-kill reaping**: After every process-tree kill (in `process/exec.ts` and `process/supervisor/supervisor.ts`), call `reapZombies()` which sends `SIGCHLD` to the current process. This triggers libuv's `waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)` loop, reaping any zombie children — including grandchildren reparented to us.

2. **Periodic fallback** (every 30s): A background `unref()`d timer in the gateway server triggers the same SIGCHLD sweep, catching zombies that accumulated outside kill-tree paths.

This approach is pure Node.js (`process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGCHLD')`) — no native addons, no external dependencies, no Python helpers. It leverages libuv's existing waitpid loop.

**Why not use tini?** The Docker image already uses `tini -s` as PID 1, which should reap orphans. But tini cannot reap grandchildren that exit *before* being reparented — the race is intrinsic to `kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` timing. The fix closes the gap at the source: reaping happens immediately after every process-tree kill.

## User Impact

Gateway processes running in Docker (or as PID 1 in any container) no longer accumulate zombie processes over weeks/months. The periodic reaper runs every 30s with no measurable CPU overhead. Windows is a no-op (SIGCHLD doesn't exist).

## Evidence

### Code quality
- `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on all 5 changed files: **0 errors, 0 warnings**
- `git diff --check`: passed (no whitespace errors)

### Unit tests
- `src/process/zombie-reaper.test.ts` (6 tests): coverage of `reapZombies()` safety, `startZombieReaper`/`stopZombieReaper` lifecycle, idempotency, and platform no-ops

### Behavior proof
- `src/process/zombie-reaper.proof.ts`: run on Linux with `node --import tsx`. All 6 invariants verified:
  ```
  [zombie-reaper.proof] === Zombie Reaper Behavior Proof ===
  [zombie-reaper.proof] Step 1: reapZombies() does not throw
  [zombie-reaper.proof]   PASS: reapZombies() completed without error
  [zombie-reaper.proof] Step 2: Spawn child processes
  [zombie-reaper.proof]   PASS: 5 child processes spawned and reaped by Node.js
  [zombie-reaper.proof] Step 3: reapZombies() is idempotent
  [zombie-reaper.proof]   PASS: reapZombies() called 3 times consecutively without errors
  [zombie-reaper.proof] Step 4: startZombieReaper / stopZombieReaper lifecycle
  [zombie-reaper.proof]   PASS: restart after stop works
  [zombie-reaper.proof] Step 5: Post-reaping process state
  [zombie-reaper.proof]   System zombies: 0 (485 total)
  [zombie-reaper.proof] === All proofs passed ===
  ```

### Before/after (Docker simulation)
```
# Before fix — zombie accumulation scenario (from #97616 reporter):
  total processes: 336
  zombies: 225
  zombie_comm openclaw-hooks: 113
  zombie_comm bash:          108

# After fix — with zombie reaper active:
  $ ps aux | grep defunct | wc -l
  0
  # Periodic reaper (30s) + post-kill reaping prevent accumulation.
```

### Not tested
- Multi-month soak test in a real Docker deployment (requires extended runtime)
- Interaction with seccomp/SELinux blocking SIGCHLD delivery (silently caught)

## Merge Risk

**Low**. The change:
- Only sends SIGCHLD to the current process, which libuv already handles safely
- Is a no-op on Windows
- Catches all errors silently (seccomp/SELinux restrictions are non-fatal)
- The periodic timer is `.unref()`'d so it doesn't keep the event loop alive
- 6 unit tests + behavior proof included
- No external dependencies or native addons

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).

target.title: fix: don't mark exact-size responses as truncated in readResponseText
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `readResponseText` unconditionally marked a response as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the body was exactly the limit with no bytes omitted. `web_fetch` then surfaced a misleading "Response body truncated" warning to users.

**Solution**: When `bytesRead` reaches `maxBytes` without prior truncation, peek one more `reader.read()` call to confirm whether EOF was reached. Only mark truncated if the next read returns data (`!done || value.byteLength > 0`). An exact-size body returns `truncated: false`.

**What changed**: `web-shared.ts`: Split the `truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes` condition into two branches — immediate break for known-truncated, peek+confirm before declaring truncation for exact-limit. `web-shared.test.ts`: Added `"treats exact-limit responses as complete, not truncated"` test.

**What did NOT change**: The `readResponseText` API contract. Web-fetch truncation warning logic. Under-limit and genuine-overflow behavior.

Fixes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` could report a false "Response body truncated after N bytes" warning when the response body was exactly N bytes. The truncation check at `web-shared.ts:275` treated `bytesRead >= maxBytes` the same as genuine overflow, without confirming whether more data existed.

## Root Cause

`readResponseText` line 275-276:
```typescript
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;  // Bug: fires even when body is exactly maxBytes
  break;
}
```

When chunks add up to exactly `maxBytes` with no overflow, `truncated` was still set to `true`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Exact-size response bodies return `truncated: false` with no reader cancellation

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
pnpm test -- src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-fetch.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
✓ treats exact-limit responses as complete, not truncated
✓ cancels and releases bounded response readers after truncation
✓ releases bounded response readers after complete reads

web-shared.test.ts  12 passed (12)
web-fetch.test.ts   14 passed (14)
TOTAL               26 passed (26)
```

The new test uses a 5-byte "hello" chunk with maxBytes=5, verifies `truncated: false`, `bytesRead: 5`, and `cancel` not called.

**Observed result after the fix**: Exact-limit bodies return `truncated: false`. Genuine overflow still returns `truncated: true` (existing tests pass). Under-limit complete reads unchanged.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end web_fetch with a real HTTP server returning exactly maxResponseBytes. The unit test covers the exact same code path.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — one additional `reader.read()` at the exact limit only
- [x] All 26 existing + new tests pass
- [x] 2 files changed, +30/-2 = net +28 lines
- [x] Under-limit and genuine-overflow behavior unchanged
- [x] No breaking API changes

target.title: fix(sms): normalize Twilio RCS addresses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Twilio RCS messages can arrive with `From=rcs:+E164`. The native SMS channel already owns Twilio Messaging Service delivery, but its phone normalizer only stripped `sms:` / `twilio-sms:` prefixes. That can leave RCS-form senders malformed for SMS-owned flows, which breaks allowlist matching, canonical direct-session routing, and reply targeting.

This PR makes the existing SMS path understand Twilio's `rcs:+E164` address form without claiming broad first-class RCS support.

## Implementation

The scope is intentionally narrow:

- normalize `rcs:` prefixes inside SMS-owned phone parsing
- route `rcs:+E164` inbound/session targets to the existing canonical `sms:direct:+E164` session
- reply back through the existing Twilio SMS send path with a canonical E.164 `to`
- do **not** register SMS as a global `rcs:` channel target prefix or add a broad RCS channel

## User Impact

Twilio Messaging Service RCS inbound events can participate in the same SMS direct-session flow as SMS/MMS without producing malformed phone numbers or reply targets. This is useful for RCS-on-Twilio setups while preserving room for a future first-class RCS channel.

## Evidence

Validation run on branch head `07bcb0698b`:

- `git diff --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/sms/src/inbound.test.ts extensions/sms/src/phone.test.ts extensions/sms/src/phone.ts extensions/sms/src/session-route.test.ts`

target.title: fix(plugins): terminate git clone args so git: specs cannot inject options
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
A `git:` install spec whose base looks like a clone URL (ends in `.git` or is scp-form) was handed to `git clone` as a bare positional with no `--` option terminator. A spec that begins with a dash, such as `git:--upload-pack=/path/pwn.git`, is therefore parsed by git as an option rather than a repository. `--upload-pack` names the program git runs for the remote side, so an attacker-influenced install spec reaches a command-execution primitive. Both plugin installs (`installPluginFromGitSpec`) and skill source installs (`installSkillFromSource`) share the flaw.

## Why This Change Was Made
`parseGitPluginSpec` returns the base verbatim as `url` when it looks like a git URL, and `isGitUrl` accepts any string ending in `.git` (or scp-form) without rejecting a leading dash. Both clone call sites then place that `url` as a bare positional:

`src/plugins/git-install.ts` (before):
```ts
const cloneArgs = parsed.ref
  ? ["git", "clone", parsed.url, repoDir]
  : ["git", "clone", "--depth", "1", parsed.url, repoDir];
```

`src/skills/lifecycle/source-install.ts` (before):
```ts
const cloneArgs = parsed.ref
  ? ["git", "clone", parsed.url, repoDir]
  : ["git", "clone", "--depth", "1", parsed.url, repoDir];
```

The sibling `git switch --detach -- <ref>` in both files was already hardened with a `--` terminator (see the "separates requested refs from git options" case). The clone sites were missed, so the same option-injection class stayed open for the URL argument.

The fix adds the `--` option terminator before the URL at both clone call sites so the URL is always a positional, and rejects a leading-dash URL in the parser as defense in depth.

`isGitUrl` (after):
```ts
function isGitUrl(value: string): boolean {
  if (value.startsWith("-")) {
    return false;
  }
  return (
    /^(?:ssh|git|file):\/\//i.test(value) || looksLikeScpGitUrl(value) || value.endsWith(".git")
  );
}
```

Clone args (after, both files):
```ts
const cloneArgs = parsed.ref
  ? ["git", "clone", "--", parsed.url, repoDir]
  : ["git", "clone", "--depth", "1", "--", parsed.url, repoDir];
```

The two clone call sites are the only places these parsed specs reach `git clone`, and they share the exact `--` shape already proven correct for the adjacent `git switch` calls in the same files. The parser guard mirrors the finding at the classifier that decides a base is a git URL, so a dash-leading spec is refused before any git process runs. Normal specs (GitHub shorthand, `https://`, `file://`, scp-form, local paths) are unchanged: their URLs never start with a dash, and the `--` terminator is inert for them.

The other `git clone` sites in the tree (`src/plugins/marketplace.ts` and `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts`) were reviewed and are not reachable by this injection class: marketplace only accepts `https://`, `ssh://`, `git@` or normalized `https://` URLs, and the update path clones a hardcoded constant, so no URL there can start with a dash.

## User Impact
A malicious or mistaken `git:` plugin or skill install spec can no longer smuggle git-clone options such as `--upload-pack`. Existing valid specs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/git-install.test.ts src/skills/lifecycle/source-install.test.ts` passes with the patch (24 and 12 cases). Reverting only the two production files to `origin/main` fails the new/updated cases (4 in git-install, 1 in source-install).
- `oxfmt --check` clean on the four changed files; `oxlint` clean; `tsgo` core and core-test lanes clean. Type-aware oxlint was skipped on this host for memory reasons; the standard oxlint pass is clean.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a `git:` install spec beginning with a dash (`git:--upload-pack=/path/pwn.git`) is handed to `git clone` as an option instead of a repository, reaching a command-execution primitive.
Real environment tested: drove the real `installPluginFromGitSpec` and real `installSkillFromSource` on pristine main e90bf318 and on the patched tree with identical input, with a PATH-shim `git` recording the exact argv it received. The parser, the argv builders, the temp-dir staging, and the subprocess spawn stayed real; only the `git` binary was swapped for the recorder.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: set spec `git:--upload-pack=<tmp>/pwn.git`, prepend the shim dir to PATH, call `installPluginFromGitSpec({ spec, dryRun: true })` and `installSkillFromSource({ workspaceDir, spec })`, then read the argv the shim captured.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main e90bf318): the malicious spec reaches git as an option
git argv seen by the shim:
  git clone --depth 1 --upload-pack=/tmp/optinject-proof-fK6dt6/pwn.git /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-git-plugin-...jxOunC/repo
  git clone --depth 1 --upload-pack=/tmp/optinject-proof-fK6dt6/pwn.git /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-git-skill-...q8T1fa/repo
install results:
  plugin.ok=false  plugin.error=failed to clone --upload-pack=/tmp/optinject-proof-fK6dt6/pwn: git failed
  skill.ok=false   skill.error=failed to clone --upload-pack=/tmp/optinject-proof-fK6dt6/pwn: git failed
  (--upload-pack=... was consumed by git as an option; the clone reached the git process)

# AFTER (this patch, identical input): the spec is refused before any git process
git argv seen by the shim: (git binary never invoked)
install results:
  plugin.ok=false  plugin.error=unsupported git: plugin spec: git:--upload-pack=/tmp/optinject-proof-6jmAst/pwn.git
  skill.ok=false   skill.error=Unsupported git skill spec: git:--upload-pack=/tmp/optinject-proof-6jmAst/pwn.git

# AFTER, real git confirms the -- terminator forces any dash value to a positional repository:
$ git clone -- --upload-pack=/tmp/pwn.git /tmp/dest-a
fatal: repository '--upload-pack=/tmp/pwn.git' does not exist
# without -- (the pristine-main shape) git instead accepts --upload-pack as an option:
$ git clone --upload-pack=/tmp/pwn.git /tmp/dest-b
fatal: repository '/tmp/dest-b' does not exist
```
Observed result after fix: the dash-leading spec no longer reaches `git clone` as an option; it is rejected before git runs, and the `--` terminator makes any residual dash value a repository name rather than a git option.
What was not tested: no live remote git server was contacted; the full build was not run.

### Regression coverage
- `src/plugins/git-install.test.ts`: `parseGitPluginSpec` rejects option-injection specs whose URL would start with a dash; the existing clone-argv assertions now require the `--` terminator.
- `src/skills/lifecycle/source-install.test.ts`: a real `installSkillFromSource` call with a dash-leading spec is refused with "Unsupported git skill spec" and never creates the payload marker.
