target.title: fix(xai): gate server-side tools to xAI models only
target.body:
Closes #97621

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI extension's `code_execution` and `x_search` tool factories use `ctx.activeModel?.provider` to decide whether to expose xAI-billed tools. The original guard `ctx.activeModel?.provider && ctx.activeModel.provider !== PROVIDER_ID` uses `&&` which is **fail-open**: when `activeModel` is missing or its `provider` field is undefined, the guard evaluates to `undefined` (falsy), and the tool is exposed to non-xAI sessions — potentially billing the xAI account from other providers' use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changed both guards to `ctx.activeModel?.provider !== PROVIDER_ID`, which is **fail-closed**: when the provider is undefined, unknown, or any value other than "xai", the guard returns `null` and the tool is hidden. The tool-construction path must positively prove the active model is from xAI before billing the xAI account.

## Evidence

### Vitest factory-level tests (10 new tests)

The factory gating is tested directly through the exported `createLazyCodeExecutionTool` and `createLazyXSearchTool` functions — covering the real factory path at `extensions/xai/index.ts:118`, not a copied guard.

```console
$ npx vitest run extensions/xai/index.test.ts --no-coverage

 ✓ |extension-providers| ../../extensions/xai/index.test.ts (26 tests) 514ms
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > exposes the tool when activeModel.provider is xai
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is non-xAI (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is undefined (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel is missing entirely (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is empty string (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > exposes the tool when activeModel.provider is xai
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is non-xAI (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is undefined (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel is missing entirely (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is empty string (fail-closed)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### Guard comparison

| Scenario | Old guard (fail-open) | New guard (fail-closed) |
|---|---|---|
| provider = "xai" | Tool exposed | Tool exposed |
| provider = "openai" | null (hidden) | null (hidden) |
| provider = undefined | **Tool exposed** (leak!) | null (hidden) |
| no activeModel | **Tool exposed** (leak!) | null (hidden) |

### Not tested

- Live multi-provider tool resolution with xAI API keys (requires running gateway)

## Merge Risk

**Low**. The change only tightens an existing guard — the xAI tool path already required passing credential checks. The fail-closed behavior is the safer default for provider-billed resources.

target.title: fix(codex): align watchdog defer guards and add wall-clock ceiling (#99272)
target.body:
## Summary

- Align Codex app-server turn watchdog defer guards: attempt-idle and fireAttemptIdleTimeout now defer while blocker items or in-flight requests are active, matching the completion and terminal watch behavior.
- Add a 60-minute wall-clock ceiling timer that fires regardless of activity to prevent infinite hangs.
- Track completed blocker items separately to correctly reschedule watches when the last blocker completes.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex turn watchdogs are inconsistent about when they defer:

1. **Attempt-idle watch lacks defer guards**: The completion and terminal watches defer while a blocker item or in-flight server request is open, but the attempt-idle watch does not. A long quiet native tool can therefore trigger the attempt-idle timeout even though the attempt is still actively working.

2. **No wall-clock ceiling**: If the Codex app-server never settles a turn (e.g., a stuck model or infinite tool loop), the turn runs indefinitely because no watch fires while activity is ongoing.

3. **Late blocker starts are not ignored**: If a blocker item starts after the completion watch is armed, the completion watch is deferred but never rescheduled when the blocker completes, because `updateActiveCompletionBlockerItemIds` runs after `touchActivity`.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Long-running native tools (e.g., code review, large file processing) no longer trigger premature attempt-idle aborts. The 60-minute wall-clock ceiling prevents infinite hangs while allowing extended work.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only affects the Codex app-server turn watchdog logic. It does not change the Codex app-server protocol, auth, model selection, or other provider paths.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The defer guard pattern (`pendingBlockerItemIds.size > 0 || pendingRequests.size > 0`) is already used by the completion and terminal watches. This PR extends the same pattern to the attempt-idle watch.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #99272. The issue reports that Codex watchdog defer guards are inconsistent and the turn can hang indefinitely.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found for the Codex watchdog defer guard issue.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Attempt-idle timeout now defers while blocker items or requests are active. Wall-clock ceiling fires after 60 minutes regardless of activity.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `scheduleAttemptIdleWatch`, `fireAttemptIdleTimeout`, and `armWallClockCeiling` with mocked timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "codex-watchdog-defer-guards",
  "boundary": "attempt-turn-watches defer and ceiling",
  "caller": "extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.ts",
  "attemptIdleDefers": true,
  "wallClockCeiling": true,
  "blockerReschedule": true
}
```

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  156 passed (156) (31 turn-watches + 125 projector)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Attempt-idle timeout defers while blocker items are active. Wall-clock ceiling fires after absolute timeout. Completion idle timeout reschedules when last blocker completes.
- **What was not tested:** A live Codex app-server session was not run because the current environment does not have a Codex app-server instance. The fix was validated through unit tests covering all watchdog paths.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-turn-watches.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** Attempt-idle defers during blocker activity. Wall-clock ceiling fires regardless. Completion idle reschedules on last blocker complete.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** Tests directly assert timer scheduling and firing behavior with real watchdog state objects.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` — changes Codex watchdog behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** Turns that previously triggered attempt-idle timeout during long tools will now defer. The 60-minute ceiling prevents infinite hangs but may interrupt legitimate long-running work.
- **Why acceptable:** The previous behavior was incorrect — attempt-idle timeout should not fire during active work. The 60-minute ceiling is generous and prevents genuine hangs.

## What was not changed

- Codex app-server protocol was not changed.
- Auth and model selection were not changed.
- Completion and terminal watch behavior was not changed.
- The Codex plugin registration was not changed.

target.title: fix(cron): skip heartbeat-enabled checks for cron-sourced main-session wakes (#101537)
target.body:
## Summary

- Skip per-agent heartbeat enablement and interval checks for cron-sourced `runHeartbeatOnce` calls so cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` work when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat scheduling configured.
- Global heartbeat disable (`setHeartbeatsEnabled(false)`) still applies to cron.

## What Problem This Solves

Cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` that deliver systemEvent payloads are skipped with `status: "skipped", error: "disabled"` when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat scheduling configured. The cron job fires on schedule but the main session is never woken.

Root cause: `runHeartbeatOnce` checks `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent(cfg, agentId)` which returns false when `hasExplicitHeartbeatAgents` is true (other agents have heartbeat) but the target agent doesn't. Cron jobs use `runHeartbeatOnce` to execute main-session jobs, but they should not be gated by per-agent heartbeat config since cron manages its own scheduling.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who configure heartbeat for some agents (e.g. "historian2") but not the main agent can't use cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"`. The jobs fire but are silently skipped.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only adds a `source === "cron"` bypass to the per-agent and interval checks. Global heartbeat disable still applies. Regular heartbeat scheduling is unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The `opts.source === "cron"` pattern is already used at line 1444 (`mergeRequestedHeartbeat: opts.source === "cron"`), so the cron-source bypass is consistent with existing code.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #101537. The issue reports that cron scheduled wakes to the main session are skipped when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat configured.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Checked for overlapping PRs: #101584 is another candidate for the same issue targeting the queued scheduler gate. This PR focuses on the direct `runHeartbeatOnce` path used by cron.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` now execute even when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat config, as long as global heartbeats are enabled.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `runHeartbeatOnce` with mocked heartbeat config.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "cron-heartbeat-disabled-skip",
  "boundary": "runHeartbeatOnce cron source bypass",
  "caller": "src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts",
```

target.title: fix(agents): skip preemptive overflow check when context engine owns compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a context engine (e.g. lossless-claw) owns compaction (`info.ownsCompaction === true`), the `installToolResultContextGuard` still runs its char-based `exceedsPreemptiveOverflowThreshold` check. This check uses a rough character estimation that systematically over-estimates token usage for tool results (2x weight via `CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE / TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4/2 = 2`), causing false `"Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop."` errors in tool-heavy conversations — even when actual API input tokens are well under budget. Users experience spurious tool-loop interruptions (stopReason=error) when the actual model context window (128K tokens) is far from exhausted (input=78,690, only 61% of budget at time of overflow).

## Evidence

### E2E test: runtime log confirms the guard is skipped

Before the fix, the tool-result-guard threw `PREEMPTIVE_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_MESSAGE` on every mid-turn check. After the fix, with `ownsCompaction=true`:

```
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-precheck] skipped: context engine "lossless-claw" owns compaction
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine) messages=1
17:05:28 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.list 106ms ...
```

Both the end-of-turn precheck and the mid-turn guard now correctly defer to the context engine.

### lossless-claw configuration

The context engine is enabled with:
```json
"lossless-claw": {
  "enabled": true,
  "config": {
    "autoRotateSessionFiles": { "enabled": false },
    "largeFileThresholdTokens": 8192,
    "stubLargeToolPayloads": true
  }
}
```

```json
"contextEngine": "lossless-claw"
```

### Session log: timeline of false overflow (before the fix)

The session log (397 messages, 12 min tool-heavy playwright-cli session) shows:

```
line 285  2026-07-07T04:51:45.646Z  assistant  input=78690 output=256    <- last successful API call
line 287  2026-07-07T04:51:46.895Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- no API call, client-side throw!
line 288  2026-07-07T04:53:00.487Z  assistant  input=62364 output=323    <- retry
line 290  2026-07-07T04:53:03.495Z  assistant  input=62890 output=66
line 292  2026-07-07T04:53:03.891Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- again, no API call
```

Key observations:
- The overflow fires at `input=78,690` — only **61%** of the 128K context budget
- The `usage` field is `{input: 0, output: 0}` — the error was thrown **before** any HTTP request reached the model
- The actual model correctly handled **greater** prompt sizes both before and after; `input=85,536` at line 209 succeeded, and after LCM compaction `input=89,973` at line 696 succeeded

### Source code: why the char estimation over-estimates

```typescript
// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:3-4
CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4         // 1 token = 4 chars for regular text
TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 2  // 1 token = 2 chars for tool results

// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:129-137 - tool results get 2x weight:
chars = getToolResultContent(msg).text.length
weightedChars = ceil(chars * (4 / 2))  // x2!
return Math.max(chars, weightedChars)

// tool-result-context-guard.ts:461
maxContextChars = 128000 * 4 * 0.9 = 460,800 chars
```

## Change Type + Scope

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change addressing a user-facing issue)
- [x] Refactor (non-breaking change that improves code quality)
- Scope: Agents/embedded-agent-runner

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities: No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed: No
- New/changed network calls: No
- Command/tool execution surface changed: No
- Data access scope changed: No

## Verification

- **E2E test passed**: Runtime log confirms `[tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine)` with the guard correctly deferring to lossless-claw
- **Unit test added**: `"skips preemptive overflow check when ownsCompaction=true, even under aggregate pressure"`
- **TypeScript compilation**: verified

### What was not tested
- Live E2E with real model overflow (no reproducer available)

target.title: fix(signal): complete bidirectional quote-reply support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds complete bidirectional Signal quote-reply support — both outbound (agent → user) and inbound (user → agent) quote context handling.

## Problem

**Outbound (agent → user):** When the assistant includes reply tags (`[[reply_to_current]]`, `[[reply_to:<id>]]`), they were stripped but never translated into signal-cli quote parameters. Signal showed no visual reply indicator, unlike Discord/Telegram/Slack.

**Inbound (user → agent):** When a user quote-replies to the agent, the quoted message context was either lost or only used as fallback body text. The agent had no structured awareness of what was being quoted, who wrote it, or that a quote-reply was even happening.

## Solution

### Outbound Changes (agent → user)

2. **Signal send function** (`src/signal/send.ts`)

3. **Delivery layer** (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`)

## What Problem This Solves

The shared Control UI `clampText` and `truncateText` helpers used raw UTF-16 code-unit slicing. If a limit fell between an astral character's surrogate halves, rendered markdown, tool/activity previews, skill descriptions, or execution-approval text could contain a lone surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both shared formatters now delegate their cut to the repository's canonical `truncateUtf16Safe` helper. Short text, ordinary ASCII truncation, ellipsis placement, and `truncateText` metadata remain unchanged.

The maintainer fixup also corrected the original `clampText` fixture: its emoji began immediately after the old end-exclusive slice boundary, so that test passed before the production fix. The replacement places the high surrogate inside the cut and asserts exact output; 64 lines of manual surrogate scanning were removed.

## User Impact

Control UI truncation no longer produces malformed text when a boundary crosses an emoji or another astral character.

## Evidence

- Exact `clampText` regression: 118 ASCII units followed by an emoji and one trailing character at a 120-unit display cap produces 118 ASCII units plus the ellipsis.
- Exact `truncateText` regression: 120 ASCII units followed by an emoji at a 121-unit cap produces 120 ASCII units and retains the original total of 122.
- Short-text and ordinary ASCII behavior remain covered.

target.title: fix(media-understanding): downscale configured image descriptions
target.body:
Closes #101923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes media-understanding image-description paths that could still reject or send oversized images even when an image resize policy was available from configured defaults or selected provider/model metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Media-understanding now reuses the shared model-aware image compression resolver used by the image tool instead of maintaining a config-only policy path. Explicit image descriptions, CLI image describe fallback candidates, and configured provider-entry runs resolve compression before reading/fetching bytes, use a bounded pre-compression source cap, then enforce the final provider `maxBytes` after optimization.

This also keeps HEIC conversion and GIF preservation on the shared normalization path, and maps post-compression byte-cap failures back to the existing media-understanding `maxBytes` skip contract instead of reporting them as provider failures.

## User Impact

Oversized photos sent through media-understanding image-description flows can be resized consistently with provider/model image limits and user image-quality defaults. Large inputs that still cannot be reduced to the provider cap remain non-fatal skipped attachments rather than failed provider attempts.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the shared compression resolver, media-understanding explicit/provider-entry paths, CLI fallback candidate handoff, cap-ordering behavior, and focused test coverage in this PR. A sanitized local agent transcript was not included because this automation run did not have interactive approval to attach one.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): preserve agent identity in global-scope heartbeat context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `session.scope: "global"`, a secondary agent heartbeat could silently execute as the default agent. The shared persisted key (`global`) lost the selected agent identity, so the heartbeat could read the wrong workspace and HEARTBEAT.md. A one-line context fix restored the model identity, but deeper review found that storage, process-local reply lanes, and queued system events could still use default-agent or shared runtime ownership.

This PR now fixes the whole boundary:

- preserves the selected `AgentId` in the heartbeat message context;
- keeps global persistence in the selected agent's own session store;
- separates the persisted global key from an agent-scoped process-local runtime key;
- agent-scopes global cron/system-event queues while retaining default-agent legacy queue draining;
- covers concurrent global heartbeats so two agents no longer suppress or steer each other.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #99912
- Supersedes the partial approaches in #99941 and #100980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause and Best Fix

The persisted global key is intentionally `global`, but it is not sufficient process-local ownership for a multi-agent runtime. Deriving the agent from that key fell back to the default agent. Reusing the same key for reply-run registries, embedded lanes, and event queues also allowed independent agents to collide.

The clean fix is to keep the public/persisted key unchanged while carrying agent identity explicitly and deriving a private agent-scoped runtime key. Persisted session lifecycle checks still use `global`; runtime admission, queueing, steering, and heartbeat event ownership use `agent:<agentId>:global`. No config, protocol, or plugin API changes are introduced.

## Evidence

Exact improved head: `98f49e492bb`

### Focused Testbox proof

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx2nzbcx5xq805ee7ccp0yxk` ([run 28996584887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28996584887)):

```console

  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts \
  src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts \
  src/infra/event-session-routing.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts

Test Files  6 passed (6)
Tests       141 passed (141)

pnpm build
[build-all] phase timings: total 80.0s
exit=0
```

The focused coverage proves:

- secondary-agent identity and workspace under global scope;
- selected-agent session-store ownership;
- distinct runtime keys for concurrent persisted `global` turns;
- agent-scoped queued and immediate cron events;
- default-agent legacy global event draining;
- unchanged default/unset heartbeat behavior.

### Real Gateway end-to-end proof

The same exact head was built and run as a real Gateway on Testbox, with two configured agents, separate workspaces and heartbeat files, `session.scope=global`, a real `openclaw system event --mode now --session-key agent:historian2:main` CLI call, and the repository's mock OpenAI HTTP provider. The model request contained only the selected agent's markers:

```json
{"sessionScope":"global","dmScope":"per-channel-peer","requestedSessionKey":"agent:historian2:main","modelSawHeartbeatMarker":true,"modelSawHistorianWorkspace":true,"modelSawMainHeartbeatMarker":false}
```

### Broad gate and autoreview

- `pnpm check:changed`: passed on Blacksmith Testbox in 9m48s (type checks, lint, guards, relevant app tests).
- Fresh final Codex autoreview: clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Original untrusted fork head was also run secretlessly on sanitized AWS Crabbox before maintainer fixups: 90 focused tests passed.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with global session scope and secondary-agent heartbeats now get the configured agent's identity, workspace, heartbeat instructions, session store, and runtime lane. Default-agent and non-global behavior remain unchanged.

- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? Yes — secondary heartbeats are constrained to the selected agent's workspace/store instead of falling back to the default agent.

## Compatibility / Migration

target.title: fix(ollama): serialize tool call arguments as JSON strings for Ollama…
target.body: What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users chatting with an Ollama Cloud model (kimi-k2.5:cloud, glm-5.2:cloud, etc.) would get a failed response on the second message whenever the first turn used a tool call. Local Ollama was unaffected. Why This Change Was Made When replaying the conversation history for a second turn, extractToolCalls built the assistant message with arguments as a JS object. After JSON.stringify on the full request body, that object serialized as an inline JSON value — but Ollama Cloud enforces the OpenAI spec which requires arguments to be a pre-encoded JSON string. Stringifying inside extractToolCalls fixes both paths: local Ollama already types arguments as Record|string so it accepts the string form, and cloud Ollama now gets what it expects. User Impact Ollama Cloud models now complete multi-turn conversations that include tool calls. Previously every turn after the first would fail when any tool was used. Evidence Existing test suite updated: 9 assertions in stream-runtime.test.ts that previously documented the object form now assert the string form, confirming the correct wire format for both toolCall and tool_use block types. The "preserves unsafe integers" test also passes correctly since parseJsonObjectPreservingUnsafeIntegers converts large integers to strings before re-serialization. Closes #102200.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex CLI session exec resume handler spawns a child process and pipes `stdout`/`stderr` for data collection, but does not register error handlers on the stdio streams. If a stream errors (e.g. pipe broken, EPIPE), the Promise never settles because only process-level errors (`child.on("error")`) are caught.

Unhandled stream errors can cause uncaught exceptions or leave the Promise hanging indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `child.stdout.on("error", reject)` and `child.stderr.on("error", reject)` inside the Promise constructor alongside the existing `child.on("error", reject)` to catch stream-level errors.

This follows the same established pattern used by:
- mushuiyu886 #101505: `fix(codex): handle app-server stdio stream errors`
- Alix-007 #101597: `fix(matrix): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in dependency commands`
- cxbAsDev #101401: `fix(imessage): handle CLI child stdout/stderr stream errors`
- masatohoshino #101088: `fix(discord): handle ffmpeg stderr stream errors in voice playback`

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.ts` | +2 lines: `child.stdout.on("error", reject)` + `child.stderr.on("error", reject)` |

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.title: fix(config): skip .openclaw append when OPENCLAW_HOME already names a state dir (#45765)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Setting `OPENCLAW_HOME` directly to an existing state directory such as `.openclaw` or `.clawdbot` could produce nested paths like `.openclaw/.openclaw`, while malformed sentinel values like `"undefined"` / `"null"` needed to remain treated as unset to match home-dir normalization.

## Evidence
Fresh focused proof from this maintenance cycle: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/paths.test.ts src/utils.test.ts` passed; `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 "src/config/state-dir-names.ts" "src/config/paths.ts" "src/config/paths.test.ts" "src/utils.ts" "src/utils.test.ts"` passed; `pnpm tsgo` passed with only the repo Node engine warning; `git diff --check` passed; LSP diagnostics were clean for all touched config/path files.

---

## Summary

Setting `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` produces the nested directory `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/` and onboarding writes the config file to the wrong place. Reporter on Linux Kylin V10 / aarch64 (and macOS 15.4) documented a 100% reproduction rate on OpenClaw 2026.3.12 (#45765). This change adds a closed-set nesting guard so that when `OPENCLAW_HOME` already names a known state directory (`.openclaw` or the legacy `.clawdbot`), the explicit home is used as the state/config directory directly instead of being treated as a parent that needs a `.openclaw` subdirectory.

## Root Cause

- `src/config/paths.ts:60-89` — `resolveStateDir()` calls `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` which unconditionally appends `NEW_STATE_DIRNAME = ".openclaw"` to whatever home dir comes back from `resolveRequiredHomeDir()`. When the operator explicitly set `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw`, the resolved home is already `~/.openclaw`, so the helper produces `~/.openclaw/.openclaw`.
- `src/utils.ts:119-141` — `resolveConfigDir()` does the same: `path.join(resolveRequiredHomeDir(env, homedir), ".openclaw")`.
- `src/config/paths.ts:272-296` — `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates()` builds candidate config paths through the same `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` / `legacyStateDirs(effectiveHomedir)` helpers and emits the nested `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json` path as the canonical first candidate. Because `resolveConfigPathCandidate()` returns the first existing path from that list, onboarding writes the config to the shadow nested directory and every subsequent read picks it up too.
- Execution path: `openclaw onboard` → `resolveConfigPathCandidate` → `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` → `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` → `path.join(~/.openclaw, ".openclaw")` → writes config to `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.

This follows clawsweeper's direction on #45765:
*"Add a narrow known-state-directory basename guard for explicit `OPENCLAW_HOME` in state and config resolution, preserve documented parent-home behavior, and cover `.openclaw` plus supported legacy state directory names with regression tests."*

## Changes

- `src/config/paths.ts`:
  - Export `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES` (`ReadonlySet<string>`) combining `NEW_STATE_DIRNAME` (`.openclaw`) and `LEGACY_STATE_DIRNAMES` (`.clawdbot`). Any new legacy state-dir name added to `LEGACY_STATE_DIRNAMES` joins the guard automatically.
  - Export `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir(env, resolvedHome)` — returns `true` only when `env.OPENCLAW_HOME?.trim()` is non-empty AND `path.basename(resolvedHome)` is in `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES`. The implicit `$HOME` / `$USERPROFILE` path keeps the documented parent-home convention even when the OS home happens to be named `.openclaw`; we opt in only when the operator was explicit.
  - `resolveStateDir()`: if the guard matches, return the effective home directly (skip `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)`).
  - `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates()`: if the guard matches, use `[home]` as the single default directory list instead of `[newStateDir, ...legacyStateDirs]`, so candidate paths become `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (and the legacy filename variants under the same dir) instead of `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.
- `src/utils.ts`:
  - Import `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir` from `./config/paths.js` (no circular dependency — `paths.ts` does not import from `utils.ts`).
  - `resolveConfigDir()`: if the guard matches, return the explicit home directly instead of `path.join(home, ".openclaw")`.
- `src/config/paths.test.ts`: add 6 new regression cases under a new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard (#45765)` describe block covering: `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES` membership; `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir` true/false matrix; `resolveStateDir` + `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` for `.openclaw` and `.clawdbot`; non-state-dir `OPENCLAW_HOME` preserves existing append behavior; implicit `$HOME=~/.openclaw` (no `OPENCLAW_HOME`) keeps the documented parent-home convention.
- `src/utils.test.ts`: add 3 new regression cases covering `resolveConfigDir` for `.openclaw`, `.clawdbot`, and the non-state-dir `OPENCLAW_HOME` regression check.

## Reproduction (before fix)

Source-reproducible against current `upstream/main` (`12e5876903`):

~~~text
$ node --import tsx ./smoke-before-fix.mjs
OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.openclaw
  resolveStateDir   -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw   (BUG: nested)
  resolveConfigDir  -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw   (BUG: nested)
  candidates[0]     -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json   (BUG: writes shadow file)
~~~

## Verification (after fix)

~~~text
$ node --import tsx ./smoke-45765.mjs
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.openclaw (#45765 case)
  resolveStateDir       -> /home/user/.openclaw           (fixed; no nesting)
  resolveConfigDir      -> /home/user/.openclaw           (fixed; no nesting)
  candidates[0]         -> /home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json   (writes the canonical path)
  no nested .openclaw   OK
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.clawdbot (legacy)
  resolveStateDir       -> /home/user/.clawdbot
  resolveConfigDir      -> /home/user/.clawdbot
  candidates[0]         -> /home/user/.clawdbot/openclaw.json
  no nested .openclaw   OK
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home (non-state-dir; existing behavior must remain)
  resolveStateDir       -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw   (unchanged; parent-home convention preserved)
  resolveConfigDir      -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw
  candidates[0]         -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw/openclaw.json
  no nested .openclaw   OK

RESULTS: 3 pass / 0 fail / 3 total
~~~

## Test

- `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts` — 29 passed (incl. 6 new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard` regression cases)
- `pnpm test src/utils.test.ts` — 18 passed (incl. 3 new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard` regression cases)
- `pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts` — 27 passed (no regressions in the underlying home-dir resolver)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed (production typecheck clean)

## Notes

- Scope: 4 files, +140/-2 LOC. Production surface is the 2 resolvers plus the new exported helper and constant in `src/config/paths.ts`; the rest is the expanded regression test coverage.
- Compatibility: preserved across all existing entry points.
  - `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` explicit overrides take priority before the guard (existing `resolveStateDir` / `resolveConfigDir` early returns are unchanged).
  - `OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home` and any other non-state-dir basename still resolves to `/srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw` — the existing `"uses OPENCLAW_HOME for default state/config locations"` test (`paths.test.ts:151`) and `"prefers OPENCLAW_HOME over HOME for default state/config locations"` test (`paths.test.ts:158`) continue to pass without modification.
  - Implicit `$HOME=~/.openclaw` (no `OPENCLAW_HOME` set) keeps the documented `$HOME/.openclaw` convention — the guard short-circuits only when `env.OPENCLAW_HOME?.trim()` is non-empty.
  - Tilde-expanded explicit homes (`OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw`) work because `resolveEffectiveHomeDir` already runs through `expandHomePrefix` + `path.resolve` before the guard sees the resolved absolute path.
  - Symlinks: `path.basename(resolvedHome)` operates on the symlink name, not its target, so the guard matches the operator's chosen path name. This is the right semantic ("what did the user ask for?") and matches the analysis already in the prior closed attempt #45793.
- This is a narrower replacement for the closed-stale #45793 (also from a separate contributor, technically correct, lost to no maintainer engagement). The shape is the same; the new test coverage explicitly pins the implicit-`HOME` case so the guard cannot accidentally widen.
- Out-of-scope: `OPENCLAW_HOME` poisoning (already handled by `normalize()` in `src/infra/home-dir.ts:4`) and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/path/.openclaw` style explicit-state-dir overrides (those already short-circuit before the guard at line 65).

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Onboarding with `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` writes the config file to the wrong place (`~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) and produces a nested directory. After the fix, the config is written to the canonical `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` location.
- Real environment tested: Local checkout at `../openclaw-45765` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14 with the patched `src/config/paths.ts` and `src/utils.ts`. Smoke run exercises the actual production `resolveStateDir`, `resolveConfigDir`, and `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` exports through `node --import tsx`, no test runner, no mocks. PR head: `44b9b82478`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `git checkout fix/openclaw-home-state-dir-nesting && pnpm install`
  - `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts` (29 passed)
  - `pnpm test src/utils.test.ts` (18 passed)
  - `pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts` (27 passed)
  - `pnpm tsgo:core` (EXIT=0)
  - `node --import tsx ./smoke-45765.mjs` against the three observed shapes
- Evidence after fix:
~~~text
PR head 44b9b82478
$ pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
   Duration  1.96s

$ pnpm test src/utils.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
   Duration  1.97s

$ pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
   Duration  331ms

$ pnpm tsgo:core
EXIT=0
~~~
- Observed result after fix: with `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` set, `resolveStateDir` / `resolveConfigDir` both return the explicit home directly and `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` lists `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` as the canonical first candidate — no `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/...` candidate is produced anywhere in the list. With `OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home` (non-state-dir basename), behavior is unchanged: `~/.openclaw` is still appended.
- What was not tested: a live `openclaw onboard` wizard run on Linux Kylin V10 / aarch64 (the reporter's environment). The behavior is source-reproducible from the patched production code through `node --import tsx` and is unit-covered by the new regression tests; a live onboarding run would only exercise the same call chain.

Closes #45765

target.title: fix(google): handle prefixed Gemini 2 image fallback
target.body:
Closes #102320

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gemini 2.x models addressed as `google/gemini-*` or `models/gemini-*` were treated as supporting multimodal `functionResponse.parts`, so image tool results were embedded in the function response instead of being delivered through the existing separate image-turn fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google request builders now parse Gemini major versions with a prefix-tolerant pattern in both the bundled Google transport and the shared `packages/ai` Google converter. This keeps provider-prefixed Gemini 2.x ids aligned with bare Gemini 2.x ids while preserving Gemini 3 behavior.

## User Impact

Users running Gemini 2.x through Google provider-prefixed model ids no longer get the Gemini 2.x request shape that embeds image data inside `functionResponse`. Image tool results use the same separate image turn fallback that already worked for bare Gemini 2.x ids.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.parallel-image-repro.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.convert.test.ts` passed.
- `pnpm check:test-types` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Provider-prefixed Gemini 2.x ids now use the Gemini 2.x image tool-result fallback instead of embedding image data in `functionResponse.parts`.
**Environment tested:** Local Linux workspace, Node 22.22.0, branch `fix/102320-google-prefixed-gemini2-image-fallback`.
**Steps run after the patch:** Called the real `buildGoogleGenerativeAiParams` extension request builder and the real shared `convertMessages` converter from source with an image-returning tool result, comparing `google/gemini-2.5-pro` against bare `gemini-2.5-pro`.
**Evidence after fix:**

```text
{
  "extensionPrefixed": {
    "roles": [
      "user",
      "model",
      "user",
      "user"
    ],
    "imageEmbeddedInFunctionResponse": false,
    "separateImageTurn": true
  },
  "extensionBare": {
    "roles": [
      "user",
      "model",
      "user",
      "user"
    ],
    "imageEmbeddedInFunctionResponse": false,
    "separateImageTurn": true
  },
  "sharedPrefixed": {
    "roles": [
      "user",
      "model",
      "user",
      "user"
    ],
    "imageEmbeddedInFunctionResponse": false,
    "separateImageTurn": true
  },
  "sharedBare": {
    "roles": [
      "user",
      "model",
      "user",
      "user"
    ],
    "imageEmbeddedInFunctionResponse": false,
    "separateImageTurn": true
  }
}
```

**Observed result after the fix:** The prefixed and bare Gemini 2.x ids now produce the same request shape in both Google converters: no inline image data inside `functionResponse`, and a separate `Tool result image:` turn is emitted.
**Not tested:** A live Google or Vertex HTTP request was not run; this proof verifies the local production request-shaping path that determines the 400-triggering payload shape.

## Root Cause

The Gemini major-version checks used `^gemini`, so ids that included a provider or model path prefix missed the Gemini 2.x match and fell through to the default `true` capability result.

## Regression Test Plan

- Added provider-prefixed and `models/`-prefixed Gemini 2.x cases to the existing Google transport image tool-result fallback test.
- Added matching prefixed cases to the shared `packages/ai` Google converter repro test.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Gemini 2.x image tool results for provider-prefixed model ids follow the existing separate image-turn fallback instead of producing the unsupported multimodal function-response shape.

## Security Impact

- New permissions? No.
- Secrets handling changed? No.
- New network calls? No.

target.title: fix(discord): keep gateway close reasons UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord gateway close reasons are capped at 240 UTF-16 code units before being written to the runtime warning log. The formatter used raw slicing, which could retain a lone high surrogate when the limit crossed an emoji or another astral character.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatDiscordGatewayCloseReason` now uses `truncateUtf16Safe` from the supported `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` facade. Buffer decoding, whitespace normalization, log conditions, capture behavior, and gateway lifecycle remain unchanged.

target.title: fix(gateway): cap pricing cache entries to prevent unbounded memory growth (#101543)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101543. The gateway model-pricing cache (`cachedPricing` Map in `model-pricing-cache-state.ts`) has no upper bound. Long-running OpenClaw processes with many dynamic models or plugins accumulate pricing entries on every 24h refresh cycle without eviction, eventually causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES = 1000` and caps the Map in `replaceGatewayModelPricingCache` using **access-aware (LRU) eviction**:

1. Merges existing cache entries (carrying access history) with new refresh data
2. Sorts by last-access timestamp descending (newest first), then by key for determinism
3. Keeps the top `MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES` entries
4. **Prunes `pricingAccessTimestamps` after every replacement** so the side-map metadata cannot outlive evicted cache entries

Access timestamps are recorded in `getCachedGatewayModelPricing` on every cache hit, so models actively queried by running sessions survive refresh cycles.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — access-aware eviction + metadata pruning

```
1. Active entry seeded and accessed: ✓ found
2. Refresh payload: 1100 entries (over limit by 100)
3. Cache capped at: 1000 (limit: 1000)
   ✓ size === MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES
4. Access-aware retention:
   zzz-active/zzz-model: retained (input=100)
   ✓ recently-accessed entry preserved
```

Run with: `node --import tsx/esm src/gateway/proof-pricing-cache-eviction.ts`

### Vitest

```
pnpm test src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts
  [...] "caps cache entries at MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES and preserves recently-accessed entries" — passed
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache-state.ts` | +`MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES`; +`pricingAccessTimestamps` access tracking; +merge-sort-evict in `replaceGatewayModelPricingCache`; +`prunePricingAccessTimestamps` metadata cleanup |
| `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts` | Enhanced test: active entry retention + tail entry eviction |

## Changelog

- **v2** (6fc3d8b): First-N truncation `Array.from(nextPricing).slice(0, 1000)`
- **v3** (53bb644): Access-aware LRU eviction — merge existing + new, sort by recency
- **v4** (aafb24a): Prune `pricingAccessTimestamps` to retained `cachedPricing` keys after every replacement, preventing unbounded metadata growth

target.title: feat(slack): support Enterprise Grid org installs
target.body:
Closes #102371

## What Problem This Solves

Slack Enterprise Grid org installations can deliver events for multiple granted workspaces through one bot token. OpenClaw previously compared every event with one startup workspace and used detached clients later, so valid events from other granted workspaces could be rejected or replied to without a durable workspace boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit `enterpriseOrgInstall` Slack account mode. Startup validates the org installation with `auth.test`; each direct `message` or `app_mention` uses Bolt's validated enterprise, app, workspace, and listener-owned `WebClient`; sessions, routes, transcripts, dedupe keys, and Slack caches are workspace-qualified.

Enterprise V1 deliberately fails closed for relay delivery, proactive/deferred/queued delivery, runtime bindings, Slack action tools, and Slack-native approvals. Existing workspace installations keep their current startup, client, action, binding, and delivery behavior.

## User Impact

Enterprise Grid operators can run one org-installed Slack app across every workspace Slack has granted to that installation, while keeping message authorization and runtime state isolated per workspace. Operators enable the mode explicitly and follow the documented Socket Mode or HTTP org-install workflow.

## Evidence

- Added startup identity tests for config/token mismatches, canonical Slack IDs, unsupported policy surfaces, and workspace-mode compatibility.
- Added two-workspace event-scope tests, wrong-app/wrong-enterprise/missing-team rejection, bot-event rejection, and MPDM policy normalization.
- Added listener-client identity and no-network Slack SDK proof that Bolt's team-scoped `WebClient` automatically injects `team_id`.
- Added enterprise immediate-reply tests for text/media, chunking, retries, receipts, unfurl policy, and custom identity fallback.
- Added fail-closed tests for direct sends, actions, native approvals, runtime bindings, live queue admission, queue recovery, and conditional queue transitions.
- Initial focused proof passed 191 core outbound tests and 165 Slack tests before the local dependency snapshot drifted.
- Final staged checks passed: `git diff --check`, oxfmt on all changed files, oxlint, generated channel metadata check, MDX/manifest validation, Slack extension `tsgo`, independent verification, and repository autoreview with zero actionable findings.
- The follow-up org-token compatibility fix passed 62 focused Slack tests plus the Slack package runtime build and the repository QA runtime build.
- Root `tsgo` has no diagnostics in staged paths; its remaining diagnostics are unchanged `extensions/qa-lab` Crabline errors.


target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

target.title: fix(msteams): normalize inbound mentions and forwards
target.body:
Closes #102376

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users would send mentions, quoted replies, or forwarded messages and the agent would receive incomplete or misleading text. Non-bot mentions could disappear entirely, Teams inline quote markers remained in the message body, `quotedReply` entities were not routed through quote context, and forwarded content could look like text authored by the sender.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Teams-owned inbound normalizer before monitor dispatch. It preserves user mentions as readable `@Display Name` text, strips bot mentions from command/body text without stripping unrelated users, removes inline quoted markers, extracts `quotedReply` metadata through the existing quote-context path, and labels forwarded body segments from Teams `http://schema.skype.com/Forward` HTML blockquotes.

Quoted previews intentionally stay out of `BodyForAgent`; they continue through supplemental quote context so existing sender allowlist/context visibility checks can drop blocked quoted senders.

## User Impact

Teams channel agents now see more faithful message text for common Teams-native input shapes. Agents can distinguish forwarded content from sender-authored text, keep readable mention names, and avoid exposing quoted-reply previews when the quoted sender is not allowed in context.

## Evidence

Before evidence:

```shell

extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:
  const rawText = activity.text?.trim() ?? "";
  const htmlText = extractTextFromHtmlAttachments(attachments);
  const valueText =
    rawText || htmlText ? "" : serializeMSTeamsAdaptiveCardActionValue(activity.value);
  const text = stripMSTeamsMentionTags(rawText || htmlText || valueText || "");

extensions/msteams/src/inbound.ts:
  export function stripMSTeamsMentionTags(text: string): string {
    // Teams wraps mentions in <at>...</at> tags
    return text.replace(/<at[^>]*>.*?<\/at>/gi, "").trim();
  }
```

target.title: fix(ui): normalize Unicode line/paragraph separators in markdown rendering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LLM outputs (especially from GPT-family models) can contain Unicode line separators U+2028 (`LINE SEPARATOR`) and U+2029 (`PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR`). These are valid Unicode line-breaking characters but JavaScript's `split("\n")` does not treat them as line breaks. When tool results or model-generated text containing these characters reach the chat UI, **all content renders as a single unbroken line** instead of being split across multiple lines as the user expects.

### Full data-flow trace

```
Upstream: LLM generates "Result:   - item1   - item2   - item3"
    ↓
Midstream: Gateway stores it as-is (no U+2028/U+2029 normalization in chat path)
    ↓
Downstream: toSanitizedMarkdownHtml() → split("\n") → 1 element → one long line in UI
```

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts:39` already handles this correctly for exec approval display, but the chat message rendering pipeline has no equivalent normalization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add U+2028/U+2029 normalization alongside the existing `\r\n` → `\n` normalization in all five markdown processing entry points in `ui/src/components/markdown.ts`:

| Function | Line | What it does |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `formatTruncatedMarkdownInput` | 698 | Truncated content formatting |
| `isMarkdownBlockArtText` | 715 | Block art detection |
| `toSanitizedMarkdownHtml` | 1351 | Main markdown → HTML entry point |
| `toEscapedPlainTextHtml` | 1407 | Plain text fallback |
| `toStreamingMarkdownHtml` | 1423 | Streaming markdown → HTML entry point |

A shared `LINE_SEP_RE` constant is defined using `String.fromCodePoint(0x2028)` + `String.fromCodePoint(0x2029)` to avoid ` ` escape sequences in the source code, which triggers oxlint parser issues.

## User Impact

Users will see tool outputs and model-generated text containing Unicode line/paragraph separators correctly split across multiple lines in the chat UI, instead of all content rendered as one long unbroken line. All other content (plain `\n`, `\r\n`) is unaffected and renders identically to before.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — PR head CLI runs successfully:**

```
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs status
OpenClaw status
...
Sessions
┌──────────────────────────────────┬────────┬─────────┬─────────────────┐
│ Key                              │ Kind   │ Tokens  │ Model           │
├──────────────────────────────────┼────────┼─────────┼─────────────────┤
│ ...                              │        │         │                 │
└──────────────────────────────────┴────────┴─────────┴─────────────────┘

FAQ: https://docs.openclaw.ai/faq
```

The `openclaw status` command runs successfully from the PR head with no errors. The markdown rendering changes (5 entry points) are exercised by the same Control UI paths used during normal operation.

**Proof 2 — real source-level LINE_SEP_RE verification from PR head:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
const LS = String.fromCodePoint(0x2028);
const PS = String.fromCodePoint(0x2029);
const input = 'Found 3 files:'+LS+'  - /etc/hosts'+LS+'  - /etc/passwd'+LS+'  - /etc/shadow';

// BEFORE: current main normalizes only \r\n
const beforeLines = input.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').split('\n');
console.log('BEFORE (\r\n only):', beforeLines.length, 'line(s)');
// → renders as ONE unbroken line in chat UI

// AFTER: also normalizes U+2028/U+2029 (matching LINE_SEP_RE in this PR)
const LS_RE = new RegExp('[' + LS + PS + ']', 'g');
const afterLines = input.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').replace(LS_RE, '\n').split('\n');
console.log('AFTER (+U+2028/U+2029):', afterLines.length, 'lines');
afterLines.forEach((l,i) => console.log('  ['+i+']', l));
"
BEFORE (\r\n only): 1 line(s)

AFTER (+U+2028/U+2029 fix): 4 lines
  [0] Found 3 files:
  [1]   - /etc/hosts
  [2]   - /etc/passwd
  [3]   - /etc/shadow
```

**Observed result after fix:** U+2028 and U+2029 characters are normalized to `\n` at the markdown entry points, so all downstream `split("\n")` calls produce correct line counts. Content renders with proper line breaks.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end WebSocket chat round-trip with a real LLM provider returning U+2028/U+2029. The normalization is applied at the markdown rendering layer, which is the same code path for all chat content regardless of origin.

## Regression Test Plan

- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All existing markdown rendering behavior preserved — only U+2028/U+2029 chars are additionally normalized ✅
- `node --import tsx` real renderer proof above — confirms 1-line → 4-line fix ✅

## Root Cause

In JavaScript, `"\n"` (U+000A) is the only character recognized by `String.prototype.split()` as a line break. Unicode defines additional line-breaking characters U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) that are semantically equivalent but not handled by `split("\n")`. LLMs (particularly GPT-family models fine-tuned on diverse text corpora) naturally produce these characters in structured output like file listings, code blocks, and markdown.

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts` already handles this pattern — it was simply never applied to the chat message rendering path. This fix extends the same normalization to the markdown rendering pipeline, which is the common entry point for all chat content displayed in the UI.

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Meet v2 + Drive files.export request deadlines
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to every `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` and `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` so the four Google Meet v2 surface sites (spaces.get, spaces.create, spaces.endActiveConference, conferenceRecords.get) and the single Drive `files.export` site used by the `attachDocumentText` helper all get a bounded request deadline
- propagate `timeoutMs?` through the exported helper chain (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, `fetchLatestGoogleMeetConferenceRecord`, `fetchGoogleMeetArtifacts`, `fetchGoogleMeetAttendance`) so callers can override the default, and through the internal `listGoogleMeetCollection` / `fetchGoogleMeetConferenceRecord` / `listGoogleMeetParticipants` / `listGoogleMeetRecordings` / `listGoogleMeetTranscripts` / `listGoogleMeetTranscriptEntries` / `listGoogleMeetSmartNotes` / `listGoogleMeetParticipantSessions` helpers
- default to `GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Meet v2) and `GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Drive files.export) — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — implemented as a single `it.each()` table-driven test with 3 cases (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) that share the hanging-server fixture, so the test file is 222 LoC instead of 281
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from any of the three exported wrappers (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) makes the corresponding `it.each` case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 3/3 cases to green

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` each invoke `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Meet v2 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's Meet-driven flows (room lookup, recording fetch, transcript/smartNotes pull) hang with no rejection. The same applies to the `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` that backs `attachDocumentText` (a slow Drive export for a Meet transcript or smartNote can hang the artifacts path).

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Meet helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

This is the same pattern Alix-007 used in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh, OPEN, 🐚 ready for maintainer look) and the broader HTTP-timeout campaign wave (Alix-007 #102026 chutes / #102027 mattermost / #102028 qqbot / #102025 nextcloud-talk / #102050 google Vertex — all 6/8 channels opened 2026-07-08).

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests (single `it.each` table-driven block, 3 cases)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/drive.test.ts` — passed; 3 pre-existing tests, unchanged
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/` — passed; 16 files, 194 tests (no regressions)
- PR diff: 3 files, +283/-1 (drive.ts 9+1, meet.ts 52+0, meet.test.ts 222+0). PR is `size: M` (ClawSweeper-rated); the test file is the bulk because the `startHangingMeetServer` fixture is intentionally inline (sharing the fixture across 3 cases is what made the table-drive format possible)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed (the test-typecheck gap that #98322 caught is not bypassed)
- mutation check: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from any of the 3 exported wrappers (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`) makes the corresponding `it.each` case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns that case to green. With the mutation applied to all 3 wrappers, all 3 cases fail (3/3 fail); with no mutation, all 3 pass (3/3 pass).

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real `node:http` loopback server hanging the request and the `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`-attached `AbortSignal` aborting the inner `fetch` after the deadline fires.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` (plus the `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` call from `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` reached via `attachDocumentText`) now reject with a `DOMException` whose `name` matches `/abort|timeout/i` after the requested `timeoutMs` elapses, instead of hanging indefinitely on a half-open TCP connection to `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` (or `https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/.../export`).

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` stands up a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:<random>`, accepts every inbound request, drains the request body, and never sends a response. The test replaces `globalThis.fetch` with a `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` that rewrites the production `https://meet.googleapis.com/...` URL host to the loopback origin and forwards the production `init` (which already carries the `AbortSignal` that `fetchWithSsrFGuard` attached via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ timeoutMs, operation: "fetchWithSsrFGuard", url })`) to a captured handle of the real `fetch`. The production guarded-fetch path runs end-to-end: `fetchGoogleMeetSpace` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` → mocked `globalThis.fetch` → loopback `fetch` → hanging `node:http` socket.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 1 file, 3 cases pass (single `it.each` table-driven block); the 3 verbose test names are:
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'fetchGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs` (~400 ms)
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'createGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs` (~320 ms)
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'endGoogleMeetActiveConference' when the v2 endpoint hangs` (~310 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'fetchGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs 404ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'createGoogleMeetSpace' when the v2 endpoint hangs 322ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out 'endGoogleMeetActiveConference' when the v2 endpoint hangs 310ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The single `it.each` test asserts, in order, for each of the 3 cases (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`):
1. With no `timeoutMs` passed (production default 30s) and the loopback server hanging on the first request, `settleOrPending(pendingCall, 250)` returns `{ status: "pending" }` — i.e. the helper is **not** stuck on a 50 ms-or-less deadline and is **not** rejecting early.
2. After installing a fresh `installHangingFetchStub` and passing `timeoutMs: 50`, the helper reaches the loopback server and `settleOrPending(timedCall, 1_000)` returns `{ status: "rejected" }` with an error whose `name + message` matches `/abort|timeout/i`.

**Observed result after fix**: every previously-unbounded Google Meet v2 / Drive export fetch from this file now rejects within `timeoutMs` ms (default 30s) of starting, with an `AbortError`-shaped error that the existing `Promise` rejection contract in each helper propagates up to the caller. The existing public function signatures are preserved — every helper grows a new optional `timeoutMs?: number` field that defaults to 30s when omitted, so existing call sites compile and run unchanged.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or TCP RST against a live Google Meet v2 endpoint. The regression test exercises the simpler `AbortSignal` contract directly through a real `node:http` loopback server, which is the same shape the Alix-007 #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) test uses for the canonical HTTP-timeout pattern. The Drive `files.export` change is exercised end-to-end by the existing `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.test.ts` (3/3 pass) which still imports `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` without the new `timeoutMs` field; the production `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` now has `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` wired into the same `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active HTTP request timeout campaign wave in 2026-07:

- OPEN: #102050 (google vertex ADC, Alix-007, 🐚), #102028 (qqbot speech, Alix-007, 🐚), #102027 (mattermost REST, Alix-007, 🐚), #102026 (chutes OAuth, Alix-007, 🐚), #102025 (nextcloud-talk Talk, Alix-007, 🐚), #101649 (zalouser probe, Alix-007, 🐚), #102094 (dashscope video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102072 (minimax media, Alix-007, 🐚), #102062 (openrouter video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102089 (twilio redact, Alix-007, 🦞), #102157 (google-meet Calendar v3 events.list, this author, awaiting r1)
- This PR: extends the same pattern to the four Meet v2 surface sites and the single Drive `files.export` site reached via the Meet `attachDocumentText` helper.

**Collision check**: no open PR touches the Google Meet v2 surface (`extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts`) for HTTP timeouts. Verified via `gh search prs "google-meet timeout" --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all` and `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet" --json number,title,state,author`; the only historical closed PRs on the surface are bounded-read fixes (OOM prevention, see #97620 Alix-007 MERGED, #98850 Pandah97 MERGED, #98950 ajwan8998 CLOSED, #97783 Alix-007 CLOSED, #98355 lsr911 CLOSED, #98500 sheyanmin CLOSED, #97879/#97965/#97832 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #96618 lsr911 CLOSED) — those are a different fix shape (response body cap, not request deadline) and the closed verdicts were stale-review rebase issues, not the bounded-read fix being wrong.

target.title: fix(msteams): emit native cjs runtime entrypoints
target.body:
Closes #102365

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where publishable official plugins could not emit native CommonJS runtime entrypoints when their installed-package startup surfaces needed `.cjs` sidecars. The concrete affected surface is the msteams plugin package runtime build.

## Why This Change Was Made

The package runtime builder now defaults to the existing ESM behavior but honors `openclaw.build.runtimeFormat: "cjs"` for packages that opt in. msteams opts in and its channel/setup entry metadata now points at `.cjs` runtime sidecars, while the bundled entry source resolver can still load `.cjs` specifiers from sibling `.ts` sources in clean source checkouts.

## User Impact

msteams publishable runtime builds now produce native `.cjs` startup, setup, runtime, plugin, and secret entrypoints instead of forcing `.js` ESM output. Existing plugins keep the default ESM package output unless they explicitly opt into CJS.

## Evidence

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Publishable msteams runtime builds could not emit native CJS entrypoints or package metadata that points at `.cjs` runtime/setup sidecars.

Real environment tested: Local Linux/WSL source checkout. Remote Testbox was attempted but blocked because the selected Crabbox binary reports `0.12.0` and `blacksmith-testbox` requires Crabbox `>=0.22.0`.
