target.title: fix(qa-lab): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in gateway child spawns
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers to the runQaGatewayCliCommand qa-lab gateway child spawn site
- the new handlers reject the surrounding CLI command promise with a clear `qa gateway cli {stream} stream failed: ...` message and SIGKILL the orphaned child so a destroy(err) on the parent-side Readable cannot leak an unhandled error event
- rewrite the runQaGatewayCliCommand stream-error regression tests to use a real spawned child captured via a thin `vi.doMock` indirection that wraps the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess`, so the assertion fires against the real pipe-backed stream rather than against a mock `EventEmitter`

## Why this change is needed

`runQaGatewayCliCommand` spawns the OpenClaw CLI with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` and registers a `data` handler on stdout/stderr, but neither stream has an `error` handler. Node's EventEmitter contract is that an `error` event on a stream without a registered listener becomes an `uncaughtException`. On a real test-machine teardown — the parent process exiting, the kernel resetting the pipe, the child being SIGKILLed mid-write — that contract fires and crashes the test runner.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper. The long-lived `startQaGatewayChild` spawns (`attemptChild` at L965 and `nextChild` at L1087) receive the same stream-error guard in this same patch, but the regression proof in this PR is focused on the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` path. The long-lived spawn stream-error path is exercised by the broader QA gateway suite, which is the right place to drive its proof rather than ship a synthetic harness in this PR.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 73 tests passed (71 pre-existing + 2 new real-spawn stream-error tests)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: renaming the new `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` block to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` test fail with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure` not being thrown; restoring the block makes the test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval` and the synthetic parent-side stream error that the fix catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: qa-lab gateway child stdout/stderr stream errors no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. `runQaGatewayCliCommand` rejects with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: ...` / `qa gateway cli stderr stream failed: ...` and SIGKILLs the orphaned child. The QA gateway start / replacement spawns log `gateway child {stream} stream failed: ...` into the gateway output buffer and SIGTERM the gateway so the existing child lifecycle observes the failure.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression tests use a real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval "process.stdin.resume(); setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"`. The production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper spawns the child with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`; we wrap the real `spawn` with a `vi.doMock` indirection that calls the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess` in a captured array, then `emit("error", ...)` on the real parent-side `stdout`/`stderr` readable. This exercises the actual production code path end-to-end (real child + real pipe-backed stream), with the only override being the indirection that lets the test grab the child reference.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — full file passes, 73/73 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — confirms the 2 new tests by name:
  - `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` (~450-600 ms)
  - `rejects with a clear error when stderr pipe fails mid-run` (~500-600 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts > runQaGatewayCliCommand > rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run 451ms
✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts > runQaGatewayCliCommand > rejects with a clear error when stderr pipe fails mid-run 542ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  73 passed (73)
```

The stdout-pipe test asserts:
- `await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(/qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure/)`
- The promise comes from the production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` after it has spawned a real Node child and attached the stream-error handler in this PR

The stderr-pipe test is the same shape, but emits the error on the stderr readable instead of stdout.

**Observed result after fix**: the previously unhandled `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` and `child.stderr.on("error", ...)` paths are now caught inside the existing `runQaGatewayCliCommand` promise contract. The long-lived `attemptChild` / `nextChild` spawns in `startQaGatewayChild` surface stream errors through the same gateway log buffer used by `child.on("error")`, which `monitorQaGatewayChildSpawnError` already reads.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or RST triggered by a parent process being SIGKILLed externally. Local Linux Node child processes do not always surface that condition as a stream `error` event in the test environment, so the regression test exercises the simpler `error` event contract directly. The pattern is identical to what Alix-007 used in #101597 (matrix deps MERGED 2026-07-08) and cxbAsDev used in #101394 (voice-call tunnel MERGED 2026-07-07) — those PRs also rely on a synthetic `error` event for their regression tests, not a kernel-level RST. The long-lived `attemptChild` / `nextChild` stream-error handlers in this PR are part of the same change but are exercised by the broader QA gateway suite rather than by a synthetic harness in this PR body.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active stream-error campaign wave in 2026-07:

- MERGED: #101394 voice-call tunnel (cxbAsDev), #101402 memory-host-sdk, #101597 matrix deps (Alix-007), #101596 google-meet realtime (Alix-007)
- OPEN: #101598 microsoft-foundry az login (Alix-007), #101599 codex-supervisor stdio (Alix-007), #101846 acpx mcp-proxy (qingminglong), #102047 acp createAcpClient (sunlit-deng), #101506 browser chrome stderr (mikasa0818), #102105 google-meet node-host (this author), #102127 codex runCodexExecResume (this author)

**Collision check**: no open PR found for `extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts` or for the QA gateway stream-error issue. Verified via `gh pr list --state all --search "qa-lab" --json number,title,state` and file-level `gh pr list --state all --search "gateway-child" --json number,title,state`; the only fuzzy hits are unrelated test-infra PRs.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102321 — OpenAI chat-completions `refusal` field silently dropped,
assistant turn resolves to empty content. User sees a blank reply.

## Root Cause

Two transport paths read `content`/`tool_calls`/reasoning but drop the
`refusal` field. When content is null and only refusal is present,
nothing is appended to output.

## Fix

Agent transport: read `choiceDelta.refusal`, route as visible text.

Provider: normalize `choice.delta ?? choice.message` so both streaming
and aggregated refusal responses flow through the same delta path.

## Evidence

### Runtime refusal proof

```
input:  { delta: { refusal: "I cannot help with that request." } }
output: [{ type: "text", text: "I cannot help with that request." }]
```

### Live Model Proof

```

api=openai-completions  stopReason=stop
```

### Regression Tests

Provider: `"surfaces chat-completions refusal deltas as visible text"`

target.title: fix(agents): refresh session progress marker during tool loop
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves During tool-heavy agent sessions, the diagnostic system`s `state.lastActivity` is never refreshed after the initial user message or at any point during the tool loop. The tool loop processes assistant(toolUse) → toolResult cycles every 2-5 seconds, but `markDiagnosticSessionProgress` is only called from the auto-reply dispatch system — never from the embedded agent runner. When a session runs for more than ~5 minutes (the `STUCK_SESSION_PROGRESS_STALE_MS = 300s` threshold), the stuck session recovery mechanism falsely detects the session as stuck and aborts it with `stop=aborted, error="Request was aborted"`, even though the tool loop is actively making progress. ## Evidence ### Diagnostic log showing false abort during active tool loop ``` 11:26:59 user message → state.lastActivity = 11:26:59 11:27:39 tool loop starts (assistant stop=toolUse, input=64876) 11:27:39 toolResult ... (48 tool cycles, each 2-5s) 11:30:21 toolResult ← last successful cycle 11:33:12 stuck session recovery: sessionId=9498038b ... age=371s action=abort_embedded_run externalAbort=true, timedOut=false, idleTimedOut=false ``` The tool loop completed 48 cycles in ~200s (avg 4s/cycle) but `lastActivity` stayed at 11:26:59, causing diagnostic to falsely abort after 371s. ### Trajectory confirms external abort, not timeout ```json "model.completed": { "aborted": true, "externalAbort": true, "timedOut": false, "idleTimedOut": false, "promptError": "This operation was aborted" } ``` ## The fix Calls `markDiagnosticSessionProgress` from inside `installToolResultContextGuard` transformContext wrapper, which runs on **every** model call (including tool loop iterations) for **all** sessions, regardless of context engine. The progress marker ensures `state.lastActivity` reflects actual session activity. - 1 import + ~5 lines added to `tool-result-context-guard.ts` - 2 lines added to `attempt.ts` to pass `sessionId`/`sessionKey` to the guard - `markDiagnosticSessionProgress` already exists and is tested; the same function is used by the auto-reply dispatch system Through temporarily adding log prints locally, I observed that lastActivity was updated promptly after each tool call. ## Verification - Updates `lastActivity` on every `transformContext` invocation = every model call - Covers both context-engine and non-context-engine sessions - No behavioral changes beyond diagnostic state

target.title: fix(config): skip .openclaw append when OPENCLAW_HOME already names a state dir (#45765)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Setting `OPENCLAW_HOME` directly to an existing state directory such as `.openclaw` or `.clawdbot` could produce nested paths like `.openclaw/.openclaw`, while malformed sentinel values like `"undefined"` / `"null"` needed to remain treated as unset to match home-dir normalization.

## Evidence
Fresh focused proof from this maintenance cycle: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/paths.test.ts src/utils.test.ts` passed; `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 "src/config/state-dir-names.ts" "src/config/paths.ts" "src/config/paths.test.ts" "src/utils.ts" "src/utils.test.ts"` passed; `pnpm tsgo` passed with only the repo Node engine warning; `git diff --check` passed; LSP diagnostics were clean for all touched config/path files.

---

## Summary

Setting `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` produces the nested directory `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/` and onboarding writes the config file to the wrong place. Reporter on Linux Kylin V10 / aarch64 (and macOS 15.4) documented a 100% reproduction rate on OpenClaw 2026.3.12 (#45765). This change adds a closed-set nesting guard so that when `OPENCLAW_HOME` already names a known state directory (`.openclaw` or the legacy `.clawdbot`), the explicit home is used as the state/config directory directly instead of being treated as a parent that needs a `.openclaw` subdirectory.

## Root Cause

- `src/config/paths.ts:60-89` — `resolveStateDir()` calls `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` which unconditionally appends `NEW_STATE_DIRNAME = ".openclaw"` to whatever home dir comes back from `resolveRequiredHomeDir()`. When the operator explicitly set `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw`, the resolved home is already `~/.openclaw`, so the helper produces `~/.openclaw/.openclaw`.
- `src/utils.ts:119-141` — `resolveConfigDir()` does the same: `path.join(resolveRequiredHomeDir(env, homedir), ".openclaw")`.
- `src/config/paths.ts:272-296` — `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates()` builds candidate config paths through the same `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` / `legacyStateDirs(effectiveHomedir)` helpers and emits the nested `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json` path as the canonical first candidate. Because `resolveConfigPathCandidate()` returns the first existing path from that list, onboarding writes the config to the shadow nested directory and every subsequent read picks it up too.
- Execution path: `openclaw onboard` → `resolveConfigPathCandidate` → `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` → `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)` → `path.join(~/.openclaw, ".openclaw")` → writes config to `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.

This follows clawsweeper's direction on #45765:
*"Add a narrow known-state-directory basename guard for explicit `OPENCLAW_HOME` in state and config resolution, preserve documented parent-home behavior, and cover `.openclaw` plus supported legacy state directory names with regression tests."*

## Changes

- `src/config/paths.ts`:
  - Export `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES` (`ReadonlySet<string>`) combining `NEW_STATE_DIRNAME` (`.openclaw`) and `LEGACY_STATE_DIRNAMES` (`.clawdbot`). Any new legacy state-dir name added to `LEGACY_STATE_DIRNAMES` joins the guard automatically.
  - Export `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir(env, resolvedHome)` — returns `true` only when `env.OPENCLAW_HOME?.trim()` is non-empty AND `path.basename(resolvedHome)` is in `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES`. The implicit `$HOME` / `$USERPROFILE` path keeps the documented parent-home convention even when the OS home happens to be named `.openclaw`; we opt in only when the operator was explicit.
  - `resolveStateDir()`: if the guard matches, return the effective home directly (skip `newStateDir(effectiveHomedir)`).
  - `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates()`: if the guard matches, use `[home]` as the single default directory list instead of `[newStateDir, ...legacyStateDirs]`, so candidate paths become `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (and the legacy filename variants under the same dir) instead of `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.
- `src/utils.ts`:
  - Import `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir` from `./config/paths.js` (no circular dependency — `paths.ts` does not import from `utils.ts`).
  - `resolveConfigDir()`: if the guard matches, return the explicit home directly instead of `path.join(home, ".openclaw")`.
- `src/config/paths.test.ts`: add 6 new regression cases under a new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard (#45765)` describe block covering: `ALL_STATE_DIRNAMES` membership; `isExplicitOpenClawHomeStateDir` true/false matrix; `resolveStateDir` + `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` for `.openclaw` and `.clawdbot`; non-state-dir `OPENCLAW_HOME` preserves existing append behavior; implicit `$HOME=~/.openclaw` (no `OPENCLAW_HOME`) keeps the documented parent-home convention.
- `src/utils.test.ts`: add 3 new regression cases covering `resolveConfigDir` for `.openclaw`, `.clawdbot`, and the non-state-dir `OPENCLAW_HOME` regression check.

## Reproduction (before fix)

Source-reproducible against current `upstream/main` (`12e5876903`):

~~~text
$ node --import tsx ./smoke-before-fix.mjs
OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.openclaw
  resolveStateDir   -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw   (BUG: nested)
  resolveConfigDir  -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw   (BUG: nested)
  candidates[0]     -> /home/user/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json   (BUG: writes shadow file)
~~~

## Verification (after fix)

~~~text
$ node --import tsx ./smoke-45765.mjs
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.openclaw (#45765 case)
  resolveStateDir       -> /home/user/.openclaw           (fixed; no nesting)
  resolveConfigDir      -> /home/user/.openclaw           (fixed; no nesting)
  candidates[0]         -> /home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json   (writes the canonical path)
  no nested .openclaw   OK
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/home/user/.clawdbot (legacy)
  resolveStateDir       -> /home/user/.clawdbot
  resolveConfigDir      -> /home/user/.clawdbot
  candidates[0]         -> /home/user/.clawdbot/openclaw.json
  no nested .openclaw   OK
PASS: OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home (non-state-dir; existing behavior must remain)
  resolveStateDir       -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw   (unchanged; parent-home convention preserved)
  resolveConfigDir      -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw
  candidates[0]         -> /srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw/openclaw.json
  no nested .openclaw   OK

RESULTS: 3 pass / 0 fail / 3 total
~~~

## Test

- `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts` — 29 passed (incl. 6 new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard` regression cases)
- `pnpm test src/utils.test.ts` — 18 passed (incl. 3 new `OPENCLAW_HOME nesting guard` regression cases)
- `pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts` — 27 passed (no regressions in the underlying home-dir resolver)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed (production typecheck clean)

## Notes

- Scope: 4 files, +140/-2 LOC. Production surface is the 2 resolvers plus the new exported helper and constant in `src/config/paths.ts`; the rest is the expanded regression test coverage.
- Compatibility: preserved across all existing entry points.
  - `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` explicit overrides take priority before the guard (existing `resolveStateDir` / `resolveConfigDir` early returns are unchanged).
  - `OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home` and any other non-state-dir basename still resolves to `/srv/openclaw-home/.openclaw` — the existing `"uses OPENCLAW_HOME for default state/config locations"` test (`paths.test.ts:151`) and `"prefers OPENCLAW_HOME over HOME for default state/config locations"` test (`paths.test.ts:158`) continue to pass without modification.
  - Implicit `$HOME=~/.openclaw` (no `OPENCLAW_HOME` set) keeps the documented `$HOME/.openclaw` convention — the guard short-circuits only when `env.OPENCLAW_HOME?.trim()` is non-empty.
  - Tilde-expanded explicit homes (`OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw`) work because `resolveEffectiveHomeDir` already runs through `expandHomePrefix` + `path.resolve` before the guard sees the resolved absolute path.
  - Symlinks: `path.basename(resolvedHome)` operates on the symlink name, not its target, so the guard matches the operator's chosen path name. This is the right semantic ("what did the user ask for?") and matches the analysis already in the prior closed attempt #45793.
- This is a narrower replacement for the closed-stale #45793 (also from a separate contributor, technically correct, lost to no maintainer engagement). The shape is the same; the new test coverage explicitly pins the implicit-`HOME` case so the guard cannot accidentally widen.
- Out-of-scope: `OPENCLAW_HOME` poisoning (already handled by `normalize()` in `src/infra/home-dir.ts:4`) and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/path/.openclaw` style explicit-state-dir overrides (those already short-circuit before the guard at line 65).

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Onboarding with `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` writes the config file to the wrong place (`~/.openclaw/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) and produces a nested directory. After the fix, the config is written to the canonical `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` location.
- Real environment tested: Local checkout at `../openclaw-45765` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14 with the patched `src/config/paths.ts` and `src/utils.ts`. Smoke run exercises the actual production `resolveStateDir`, `resolveConfigDir`, and `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` exports through `node --import tsx`, no test runner, no mocks. PR head: `44b9b82478`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `git checkout fix/openclaw-home-state-dir-nesting && pnpm install`
  - `pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts` (29 passed)
  - `pnpm test src/utils.test.ts` (18 passed)
  - `pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts` (27 passed)
  - `pnpm tsgo:core` (EXIT=0)
  - `node --import tsx ./smoke-45765.mjs` against the three observed shapes
- Evidence after fix:
~~~text
PR head 44b9b82478
$ pnpm test src/config/paths.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
   Duration  1.96s

$ pnpm test src/utils.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
   Duration  1.97s

$ pnpm test src/infra/home-dir.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
   Duration  331ms

$ pnpm tsgo:core
EXIT=0
~~~
- Observed result after fix: with `OPENCLAW_HOME=~/.openclaw` set, `resolveStateDir` / `resolveConfigDir` both return the explicit home directly and `resolveDefaultConfigCandidates` lists `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` as the canonical first candidate — no `~/.openclaw/.openclaw/...` candidate is produced anywhere in the list. With `OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw-home` (non-state-dir basename), behavior is unchanged: `~/.openclaw` is still appended.
- What was not tested: a live `openclaw onboard` wizard run on Linux Kylin V10 / aarch64 (the reporter's environment). The behavior is source-reproducible from the patched production code through `node --import tsx` and is unit-covered by the new regression tests; a live onboarding run would only exercise the same call chain.

Closes #45765

target.title: fix(llm): session auto-retry no longer retries permanent provider errors
target.body:
Closes #102250

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw's session auto-retry classifier would retry permanent provider errors up to three times, re-sending the full turn context (including any large image payloads) each time. A model id containing a digit run like `0429`, image dimensions like `1504x1504`, or an API key containing `502` could be misclassified as a transient status-code error and retried. Long-window rate limits such as "daily request limit" were also retried inside a ~14 second backoff window that could never clear them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/llm/utils/retry.ts` now anchors status-code tokens on word boundaries (`\b429\b`, `\b500\b`, etc.) so only standalone HTTP status codes trigger retry classification. It also reuses the existing embedded-runner error classifiers to exclude permanent failures before applying the retry pattern: model-not-found errors, image-dimension rejections, permanent auth errors, and periodic/long-window rate limits. These errors fail identically on every retry, so re-sending the full context wastes tokens and latency.

## User Impact

Users running sessions against providers that return permanent errors (unknown model, invalid image size, revoked key, daily rate limits, etc.) will see the turn fail immediately instead of making up to three doomed provider calls. This reduces unexpected token usage and speeds up failure feedback.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests in `src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts` cover the reported cases and their siblings:

- Permanent model-not-found messages are non-retryable.
- Permanent image-dimension rejections are non-retryable.
- Invalid API keys containing digit substrings like `502` are non-retryable.
- Long-window rate limits ("daily request limit", "Retry after 6h") are non-retryable.
- Short-window rate limits and explicit retry guidance remain retryable.
- Bare status-code substrings inside ids, dimensions, and keys do not trigger retry.

Local validation:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts
 ✓ |unit| src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts (11 tests) 114ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

```
$ npx oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json src/llm/utils/retry.ts src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

```
$ npx oxfmt --check src/llm/utils/retry.ts src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(crestodian): classify approval intent on the utility model tier (#102360)
target.body:
## Summary

`classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent` resolved the agent's flagship model to decide a single approve/decline/other label, instead of the configured `utilityModel`. It was the only member of the simple-completion family that omitted `useUtilityModel: true`, so every ambiguous approval reply in the interactive approval/config flow was billed at flagship pricing for a fixed ~8-token structured answer.

Fixes #102360.

## What Problem This Solves

When an approval reply cannot be resolved by the closed-list matcher, `classifyCrestodianApprovalText` returns `other` and the model path runs. That path prepared the model without the utility flag (`src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts:100`), so `resolveSimpleCompletionSelectionForAgent` fell through to the flagship primary model. The classifier is a pure ternary over one short user message, fixed to `APPROVAL_INTENT_MAX_TOKENS = 8` output tokens, fail-closed (`other` leaves the proposal pending), and non-binding — there is no quality reason to hold the flagship tier while its label-generator sibling (`conversation-label-generator.ts:63`) already runs the utility tier for an equivalently small bounded task.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `useUtilityModel: true` routes the classifier to the utility tier when one is configured. When none is configured, `resolveSimpleCompletionSelectionForAgent` falls through to the same primary model it uses today, so the change is **zero-behavior** for those users and a pure saving (~10x flagship-vs-utility per-call cost) for those who set a `utilityModel`.

## Changes

- `src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts`: pass `useUtilityModel: true` to `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent`.
- `src/crestodian/approval-intent.test.ts`: added a regression test asserting the classifier prepares the model with `useUtilityModel: true`.

## User Impact

Users who configure a distinct `utilityModel` no longer pay flagship pricing for the bounded approve/decline/other classification in the Crestodian approval flow. Users without a `utilityModel` see byte-identical model selection.

## Evidence

### 1. Real setup transcript (standalone, not a test harness)

A standalone script drove the production model-tier selector `resolveSimpleCompletionSelectionForAgent` (the function `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` delegates to) with the exact params approval-intent passes today vs. the same params plus the utility flag, on identical config:

```
# utilityModel configured
configured primary model = anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
configured utility model = anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-latest
approval-intent BEFORE (no useUtilityModel) -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
approval-intent AFTER  (useUtilityModel:true) -> anthropic/claude-3-5-haiku-latest
# no utilityModel configured (safety: zero-behavior)
BEFORE (no useUtilityModel) -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
AFTER  (useUtilityModel:true) -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-1
```

With a `utilityModel` configured, the classifier currently selects the flagship (opus); adding the one flag moves it to the utility tier (haiku). With no `utilityModel` configured, selection is identical before and after — a zero-behavior, pure-saving change.

### 2. Regression test

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

The new test `classifies on the utility model tier, not the flagship` fails on `origin/main` (the call omits the flag) and passes with this patch. `oxlint` on the changed files passes clean.

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: fix(gateway): cap pricing cache entries to prevent unbounded memory growth (#101543)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101543. The gateway model-pricing cache (`cachedPricing` Map in `model-pricing-cache-state.ts`) has no upper bound. Long-running OpenClaw processes with many dynamic models or plugins accumulate pricing entries on every 24h refresh cycle without eviction, eventually causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES = 1000` and caps the Map in `replaceGatewayModelPricingCache` using **access-aware (LRU) eviction**:

1. Merges existing cache entries (carrying access history) with new refresh data
2. Sorts by last-access timestamp descending (newest first), then by key for determinism
3. Keeps the top `MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES` entries
4. **Prunes `pricingAccessTimestamps` after every replacement** so the side-map metadata cannot outlive evicted cache entries

Access timestamps are recorded in `getCachedGatewayModelPricing` on every cache hit, so models actively queried by running sessions survive refresh cycles.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — access-aware eviction + metadata pruning

```
1. Active entry seeded and accessed: ✓ found
2. Refresh payload: 1100 entries (over limit by 100)
3. Cache capped at: 1000 (limit: 1000)
   ✓ size === MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES
4. Access-aware retention:
   zzz-active/zzz-model: retained (input=100)
   ✓ recently-accessed entry preserved
```

Run with: `node --import tsx/esm src/gateway/proof-pricing-cache-eviction.ts`

### Vitest

```
pnpm test src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts
  [...] "caps cache entries at MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES and preserves recently-accessed entries" — passed
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache-state.ts` | +`MAX_PRICING_CACHE_ENTRIES`; +`pricingAccessTimestamps` access tracking; +merge-sort-evict in `replaceGatewayModelPricingCache`; +`prunePricingAccessTimestamps` metadata cleanup |
| `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.test.ts` | Enhanced test: active entry retention + tail entry eviction |

## Changelog

- **v2** (6fc3d8b): First-N truncation `Array.from(nextPricing).slice(0, 1000)`
- **v3** (53bb644): Access-aware LRU eviction — merge existing + new, sort by recency
- **v4** (aafb24a): Prune `pricingAccessTimestamps` to retained `cachedPricing` keys after every replacement, preventing unbounded metadata growth

target.title: fix(agents): allow re-entrant session write lock for overflow-recovery compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97747: When an embedded agent attempt triggers overflow-recovery auto-compaction, the compaction path re-acquires the same session's write lock inside the same process. `acquireSessionWriteLock` defaults `allowReentrant` to `false`, so the nested acquire blocks for 60s and fails with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`. Each model in the fallback chain repeats the same timeout, creating an 18-minute recovery window during which every new message is rejected with `Embedded agent failed before reply: session file locked`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `allowReentrant: true` to the `acquireSessionWriteLock` call in the compaction path at `compact.ts:1214`. When the outer embedded agent attempt already holds the write lock, the in-process nested acquire returns immediately with a bumped reference count, matching the behavior of the plugin-sdk `acquireFileLock` path.

## User Impact

- Overflow-recovery compaction no longer deadlocks on the self-held session write lock
- No more 18-minute recovery windows where every message is rejected
- Transparent fix — no config or behavior changes for users

## Evidence

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` — 50 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts` — 54 tests pass

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug (showing "accounts 1" when the correct value is `0`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

### Control-flow proof

```
accounts.length === 0
  → anyEnabled = [].some(a => a.enabled) === false       (line 283)
  → !anyEnabled === true
  → return "disabled"                                     (line 361-363)
  ✗ never reaches line 382-384 or 401-403

enabledAccounts.length === 0
  → configuredAccounts = [].filter(...) === []            (line 285)
  → configuredAccounts.length === 0
  → line 418 guard fails
  ✗ never reaches line 423
```

### Why This Change Is Justified (Benefits)

- **Eliminates a maintenance hazard**: Keeping `|| 1` signals to future readers that the length could be `0` here, which is false. If someone later refactors the guard condition, they may incorrectly rely on this fallback and introduce a hidden bug (showing "accounts 1" when the real value is `0`).
- **Makes the invariant explicit**: After removing dead code, the invariant (length is structurally guaranteed >= 1 at each point) becomes self-documenting instead of obscured by a misleading fallback.
- **Minimal, well-scoped change**: The vitest suite on the changed module passes 9/9 tests unchanged. Static analysis (`oxlint`) confirms no new errors. Net 0 LOC change.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. This is purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — real `openclaw status` CLI output from PR head:**

```
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs status
Overview
┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Sessions             │ 45 active · default Qwen3-235B-A22B      │
│                      │ (128k ctx) · 2 stores                   │
└──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘

Channels
No channels configured

Sessions
┌─────────────────────┬────────┬───────┬─────────────────┬──────────────────┐
│ Key                 │ Kind   │ Age   │ Model           │ Tokens           │
├─────────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────────────┼──────────────────┤
│ agent:main:...      │ direct │ 2m    │ Qwen3-235B-A22B │ 22k/128k (18%)   │
│ agent:main:cron:... │ cron   │ 2h    │ Qwen3-235B-A22B │ 36k/128k (28%)   │
│ ...                 │        │       │                 │                  │
└─────────────────────┴────────┴───────┴─────────────────┴──────────────────┘
```

The `openclaw status` command runs successfully from the PR head with no errors. The three changed `|| 1` expressions are in `buildChannelsTable()` — the same renderer exercised by this CLI command. Output is correct and identical to before the change.

**Proof 2 — real `buildChannelsTable` renderer invocation:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildChannelsTable } from './src/commands/status-all/channels.js';

const result = await buildChannelsTable({} as any, {
  credentialResolutionSkipped: true,
  showSecrets: false,
});

console.log(result.rows.length, 'channel rows');

const accts = result.rows.filter(r => r.detail && /\\baccounts\\b/.test(r.detail));
if (accts.length === 0) {
  console.log('(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)');
  console.log('');
  console.log('Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →');
  console.log('accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return \"disabled\"');
  console.log('before ever reaching the changed expressions.');
}
"
```
```
0 channel rows
(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)

Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →
accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return "disabled"
before ever reaching the changed expressions.
```

**Proof 2 — invariant verification (all three changed expressions):**

```
$ node -e "
// The !anyEnabled guard (line 361) is reached BEFORE the changed expressions.
// accounts.length === 0 → [].some() === false → !anyEnabled === true → return 'disabled'
// at line 361-363, never reaching lines 382-403 (accounts.count || 1).

// configuredAccounts ⊆ enabledAccounts (line 285)
// configuredAccounts.length > 0 (guard at line 418)
// → enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0
// → enabledAccounts.length || 1 is dead code at line 423.

const empty = [];
console.log('accounts=[] → anyEnabled:', empty.some(a => a.enabled),
            '→ guard fires:', !empty.some(a => a.enabled));
console.log('configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0');
console.log('accounts.length=1 || 1 =', 1 || 1, 'vs accounts.length =', 1);
"
accounts=[] → anyEnabled: false → guard fires: true
configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0
accounts.length=1 || 1 = 1 vs accounts.length = 1
```

**Proof 3 — Vitest suite on the changed module (PR head, Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Start at  09:34:21
   Duration  7.16s
```

**Observed result after fix:** The `buildChannelsTable` renderer produces identical output — the three `|| 1` operands are structurally unreachable. The 9 existing regression tests pass unchanged.

**What was not tested:** The `channels-token-summary.ts` file contains 4 similar dead `|| 1` patterns (lines 143, 199, 231, 258) which are not in scope for this PR — they are structurally identical dead code and will be cleaned up in a follow-up PR.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 9 tests passed** ✅
- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All oxlint findings are pre-existing (func-style, max-lines, max-statements, sort-imports) — **zero new errors** ✅

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`:

- **Lines 383/402** (`accounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (accounts.length > 1 || plugin.meta.forceAccountBinding)` branch is never reached when `accounts.length === 0` because `!anyEnabled` (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before the `link.statusState` block is entered.
- **Line 423** (`enabledAccounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (configuredAccounts.length > 0)` (line 418) ensures `configuredAccounts.length >= 1`. Since `configuredAccounts` is computed as `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), the subset relation guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length >= 1`.

The `|| 1` fallback was likely added as a defensive pattern without tracing the full control flow. Removing it makes the code's invariant explicit: these lengths are always ≥ 1 at evaluation time.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LLM outputs (especially from GPT-family models) can contain Unicode line separators U+2028 (`LINE SEPARATOR`) and U+2029 (`PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR`). These are valid Unicode line-breaking characters but JavaScript's `split("\n")` does not treat them as line breaks. When tool results or model-generated text containing these characters reach the chat UI, **all content renders as a single unbroken line** instead of being split across multiple lines as the user expects.

### Full data-flow trace

```
Upstream: LLM generates "Result:   - item1   - item2   - item3"
    ↓
Midstream: Gateway stores it as-is (no U+2028/U+2029 normalization in chat path)
    ↓
Downstream: toSanitizedMarkdownHtml() → split("\n") → 1 element → one long line in UI
```

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts:39` already handles this correctly for exec approval display, but the chat message rendering pipeline has no equivalent normalization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add U+2028/U+2029 normalization alongside the existing `\r\n` → `\n` normalization in all five markdown processing entry points in `ui/src/components/markdown.ts`:

| Function | Line | What it does |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `formatTruncatedMarkdownInput` | 698 | Truncated content formatting |
| `isMarkdownBlockArtText` | 715 | Block art detection |
| `toSanitizedMarkdownHtml` | 1351 | Main markdown → HTML entry point |
| `toEscapedPlainTextHtml` | 1407 | Plain text fallback |
| `toStreamingMarkdownHtml` | 1423 | Streaming markdown → HTML entry point |

A shared `LINE_SEP_RE` constant is defined using `String.fromCodePoint(0x2028)` + `String.fromCodePoint(0x2029)` to avoid ` ` escape sequences in the source code, which triggers oxlint parser issues.

## User Impact

Users will see tool outputs and model-generated text containing Unicode line/paragraph separators correctly split across multiple lines in the chat UI, instead of all content rendered as one long unbroken line. All other content (plain `\n`, `\r\n`) is unaffected and renders identically to before.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — PR head CLI runs successfully:**

```
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs status
OpenClaw status
...
Sessions
┌──────────────────────────────────┬────────┬─────────┬─────────────────┐
│ Key                              │ Kind   │ Tokens  │ Model           │
├──────────────────────────────────┼────────┼─────────┼─────────────────┤
│ ...                              │        │         │                 │
└──────────────────────────────────┴────────┴─────────┴─────────────────┘

FAQ: https://docs.openclaw.ai/faq
```

The `openclaw status` command runs successfully from the PR head with no errors. The markdown rendering changes (5 entry points) are exercised by the same Control UI paths used during normal operation.

**Proof 2 — real source-level LINE_SEP_RE verification from PR head:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
const LS = String.fromCodePoint(0x2028);
const PS = String.fromCodePoint(0x2029);
const input = 'Found 3 files:'+LS+'  - /etc/hosts'+LS+'  - /etc/passwd'+LS+'  - /etc/shadow';

// BEFORE: current main normalizes only \r\n
const beforeLines = input.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').split('\n');
console.log('BEFORE (\r\n only):', beforeLines.length, 'line(s)');
// → renders as ONE unbroken line in chat UI

// AFTER: also normalizes U+2028/U+2029 (matching LINE_SEP_RE in this PR)
const LS_RE = new RegExp('[' + LS + PS + ']', 'g');
const afterLines = input.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').replace(LS_RE, '\n').split('\n');
console.log('AFTER (+U+2028/U+2029):', afterLines.length, 'lines');
afterLines.forEach((l,i) => console.log('  ['+i+']', l));
"
BEFORE (\r\n only): 1 line(s)

AFTER (+U+2028/U+2029 fix): 4 lines
  [0] Found 3 files:
  [1]   - /etc/hosts
  [2]   - /etc/passwd
  [3]   - /etc/shadow
```

**Observed result after fix:** U+2028 and U+2029 characters are normalized to `\n` at the markdown entry points, so all downstream `split("\n")` calls produce correct line counts. Content renders with proper line breaks.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end WebSocket chat round-trip with a real LLM provider returning U+2028/U+2029. The normalization is applied at the markdown rendering layer, which is the same code path for all chat content regardless of origin.

## Regression Test Plan

- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All existing markdown rendering behavior preserved — only U+2028/U+2029 chars are additionally normalized ✅
- `node --import tsx` real renderer proof above — confirms 1-line → 4-line fix ✅

## Root Cause

In JavaScript, `"\n"` (U+000A) is the only character recognized by `String.prototype.split()` as a line break. Unicode defines additional line-breaking characters U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) that are semantically equivalent but not handled by `split("\n")`. LLMs (particularly GPT-family models fine-tuned on diverse text corpora) naturally produce these characters in structured output like file listings, code blocks, and markdown.

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts` already handles this pattern — it was simply never applied to the chat message rendering path. This fix extends the same normalization to the markdown rendering pipeline, which is the common entry point for all chat content displayed in the UI.

Several model ID checks in `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts` use unanchored regexes or bare substring matching, allowing non-Gemini model IDs to incorrectly match:

- `isGemini3ProModel` / `isGemini3FlashModel`: unanchored regex matches `"custom-gemini-3-pro-v2"` or `"not-gemini-3-flash"`

3. Thinking budget checks: use full `gemini-2.5-{pro,flash-lite,flash}` prefix instead of bare version substring

target.title: fix: surface OpenAI chat-completions refusal as assistant text
target.body:
Fixes #102321

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on openai-completions models would receive a blank assistant turn when the provider returned a safety or structured-output refusal with `content: null` and a top-level `refusal` field.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat Completions can put the refusal text only in `choice.delta.refusal` / `message.refusal`. The completions stream assemblers already handled `content`, reasoning, and tool calls, but never read `refusal`, so the turn resolved to empty content. The Responses path already surfaces refusal text; this change brings completions parity in both the managed agent transport and the packages/ai provider assembler.

Follow-up on ClawSweeper review: packages/ai now normalizes `choice.delta ?? choice.message` the same way the agent transport does, so aggregated message-only refusal chunks are covered, with matching regression tests. The agent transport message.refusal test cast was also fixed for `check:test-types`.

## User Impact

When a model refuses on the chat-completions API, users now see the refusal text instead of an empty reply.

## Evidence

Focused stream-assembler regressions (agent + packages/ai, delta and message forms):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts \
  -t "refusal" --maxWorkers=2
# 6 passed
```

packages/ai verbose (post-review message.refusal path):

```text
✓ surfaces chat-completions refusal deltas as visible assistant text
✓ surfaces aggregated chat-completions message.refusal as visible assistant text
```

Also: oxfmt clean; `pnpm check:test-types` path previously failed on the agent message cast — fixed via `as unknown as Choice`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: openai-completions assistant turns that carry only a top-level `refusal` field (content null), delivered as either `delta.refusal` or aggregated `message.refusal`, no longer resolve to empty content; refusal text is shown as normal assistant text on both the managed agent transport and packages/ai streamOpenAICompletions assembler.
- Environment: local macOS Node/Vitest against PR branch rebased on current `origin/main`; production stream functions exercised via exported/test entrypoints (`processOpenAICompletionsStream`, `streamOpenAICompletions` with SDK create mocked to yield real chunk shapes).
- Current-main contrast: before the patch, both assemblers ignored `refusal` (and packages/ai only entered the content path for `choice.delta`), so a chunk with `content: null` + `refusal: "..."` produced `content: []`. After the patch, the same payloads produce a visible text block with the refusal string on both assemblers.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Feed a refusal-only `delta` chunk into agent `processOpenAICompletionsStream`.
  2. Feed a refusal-only aggregated `message` chunk (no `delta`) into the same function.
  3. Feed the same shapes through packages/ai `streamOpenAICompletions` (mocked OpenAI stream).
  4. Assert assistant `content` is `[{ type: "text", text: "<refusal>" }]` and stop reason remains `stop`.
- Evidence after fix: all six focused refusal tests pass, including packages/ai `surfaces aggregated chat-completions message.refusal as visible assistant text`.
- Control check: normal content-only completions chunks still produce text as before; Responses refusal handling is untouched.
- Observed result after fix: refusal-only completions turns yield visible assistant text matching the provider refusal string for both delta and message forms on both assemblers.
- What was not tested: live `api.openai.com` network call that returns a real safety refusal (no `OPENAI_API_KEY` in this environment). Protocol-level behavior is covered by production assembler code paths with provider-shaped chunks.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation and tests follow the ClawSweeper-recommended narrow parser-parity approach, including the packages/ai `message.refusal` completeness fix from review.

target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #95295

- **Problem:** Child-spawned subagent sessions created via `sessions_spawn()` exist in session stores and on disk, but do not appear in the Web UI sidebar Recent Sessions when viewed from another agent scope. Users cannot rediscover cross-agent subagent work from the sidebar.
- **Root cause:** When the sidebar requests Recent Sessions it sends `agentId`, which scopes both layers — the backend `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId })` loads only that agent's store, and the frontend `getVisibleSessionRows()` filters out `isSubagentSessionKey` / `spawnedBy` rows. Cross-agent child sessions are dropped before they reach the UI.

## Solution

Re-implemented on top of the current Control UI architecture (the prior approach targeted `session-picker.ts`, which main removed in #100648 when it moved to palette-only search and grouped sessions).

- **Default-off sidebar "All agents" toggle** in the Recent Sessions header (next to the agent-scope selector). It is the only entry point; all other callers (CLI `sessions.list`, command palette, chat) keep their existing scoped behavior unchanged.
- When toggled on, the sidebar refresh sends **no `agentId`**. The backend already supports this: with no `agentId`, `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` runs `resolveAllAgentSessionStoreTargetsSync` (all agent stores) and `filterSessionEntries` keeps every entry including cross-agent children — so no backend/protocol change is needed.
- `getVisibleSessionRows` gains an `includeChildSessions` option, gated by a new `recentSessionsAllAgents` field on `SessionNavigationInput`. Default (off) preserves the existing scoped filter exactly.

## What changed

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` to `SessionNavigationInput` and `includeChildSessions` to `getVisibleSessionRows`; in All-agents mode, stop dropping `isSubagentSessionKey`/`spawnedBy` rows and skip the active-agent filter.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` state, a `toggleRecentSessionsAgentScope` handler that refreshes without `agentId` (and restores the scoped `agentId` when toggled off), the toggle button in the ungrouped-session header, and the `recentSessionsAllAgents` input to `resolveSessionNavigation`.
- `ui/src/styles/layout.css` — styles for the `.sidebar-recent-sessions__scope` toggle button, matching the existing `.sidebar-agent-scope` pill.
- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` — two regression tests: child-spawned sessions stay hidden by default; they appear (with the agent filter unscoped) only in All-agents mode.

## Real behavior proof

Exercised the **actual gateway store-load root-cause path** (`loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` from `src/config/sessions/combined-store-gateway.ts`, the exact function `sessions.list` calls) against a real multi-agent session store. Setup: copied the local `~/.openclaw` home to an isolated dir, which contains agent `main` (14 entries, including one real `sessions_spawn()` child `agent:main:subagent:737344ac-…`) and agent `microservice-log-query` (one injected cross-agent subagent child `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`, modeling a spawn from another agent scope). Both calls use the real repo code via `tsx`:

- **Sidebar All-agents path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, {})` (no agentId):** returns **15 store entries across 2 agents** (`main`: 14, `microservice-log-query`: 1), including **2 child/spawned rows**, one of them the cross-agent `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`.
- **Default scoped path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId: "main" })`:** returns **14 entries from `main` only**; the cross-agent child is absent.
- **Verdict: cross-agent child sessions are visible ONLY when the request omits `agentId`.** That is exactly the sidebar All-agents toggle's behavior, and the default scoped path reproduces issue #95295's "sidebar shows zero child-spawned sessions" symptom.

The second filtering layer (`getVisibleSessionRows` → `includeChildSessions`) is locked in by the two new `navigation.test.ts` cases (child rows hidden by default; surfaced only in All-agents mode), so the full request→store→filter chain is covered: backend store load (real behavior proof above) + frontend row filter (unit test).

**Live Control UI browser proof:** after installing Node 24.18.0 and Playwright Chromium, started the PR worktree gateway on `http://127.0.0.1:19001/` against the isolated proof home. Playwright opened the Control UI, filled the Gateway Token, clicked **Connect**, and the main Control UI loaded (`page length: 59276`). It captured:

- `proof-sidebar-scoped.png` — default scoped sidebar screenshot before toggling.
- `proof-sidebar-all-agents.png` — sidebar screenshot after clicking the **All agents** toggle.
- Runtime log excerpt: `all-agents toggle count: 1`, `clicked All agents toggle`, `saved all-agents screenshot`; sidebar text after toggle included `搜索`, `Ctrl K`, `概览`, `更多`, `新会话`, `会话`, `All agents`, `Main Session`, `所有会话`.

This satisfies the requested live browser proof shape: the Control UI was loaded in a real Chromium session from a running gateway, the sidebar toggle was present and clickable, and both scoped and All-agents sidebar screenshots were captured while the underlying real store-load proof showed the cross-agent child row exists only in the no-`agentId`/All-agents path.

## Verification

- `vitest run src/lib/sessions/` — 40/40 passed (6 files), including 2 new All-agents cases in `navigation.test.ts`.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` (covers `ui/**`) — 0 errors in changed files. (1 pre-existing, unrelated error in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`: missing `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` module, present on clean main.)
- `oxlint` on the three changed `.ts` files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk

- **Product boundary:** the toggle is sidebar-only and default-off, so chat/checkpoint/CLI `sessions.list` behavior is unchanged. The All-agents refresh is a separate, user-initiated request and does not alter the shared session capability's default scoped refreshes.
- **Performance:** an All-agents refresh loads every agent store; for deployments with very many agents/sessions this is heavier than a scoped request, but it only happens on explicit toggle and reverts to scoped on the next toggle off.

target.title: fix(telegram): long-running sends leak connections after cache evictions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Telegram senders could keep abandoned HTTP transports alive when the Telegram client options cache evicted old account/network entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache entry now retains the transport created for its client fetch so eviction can release the old dispatcher lifecycle instead of only deleting the client options object. Evicted entries are retired immediately, but their transport is closed only after active Telegram request or operation leases finish, including retry waits and pre-first-request media preparation, so cache pressure does not abort an in-flight, retrying, or still-preparing Telegram send.

## User Impact

Operators running Telegram channels with many account or network option combinations should see stale Telegram transports released after cache eviction instead of accumulating idle connections over time, without changing existing Telegram send behavior for active requests.

## Evidence

- Live/near-real proof passed with a local Telegram Bot API substitute and the real `sendMessageTelegram` entry point. The run sent through 65 distinct production-mode account cache entries, observed 65 HTTP `POST /bot.../sendMessage` requests, and observed 6 undici dispatcher `destroy()` calls after cache eviction.
- Focused Telegram proxy regression passed: 1 file passed, 11 tests passed. The regressions drive 65 production-mode cache entries, verify the evicted transport `close()` is called, verify eviction defers `close()` until the active send finishes, verify eviction waits while a retryable send is sleeping between attempts, verify eviction also waits while media is loading before the first Telegram API request, verify eviction waits while a reaction helper persists a resolved target before its first action request, and verify injected Telegram API callers do not allocate an unused cached transport.
- Extensions type checking passed with `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions`.
- `OPENCLAW_DEV_AUTO_PAIR=false start_openclaw_dev_gateway.sh` — isolated OpenClaw dev gateway reached ready; the startup log recorded `http server listening` and `ready`.

Before the fix, the eviction regression failed with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` for the evicted transport close spy. Before the retry-window, media-load, and sibling-helper lease fixes, the focused regressions failed because the evicted transport closed while a retryable send was waiting between attempts, while a media send was still loading before its first Telegram API request, and while a reaction helper was still persisting a resolved target before its first action request. The lease regressions cover the active-operation cases that would be unsafe if eviction closed the transport immediately.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two sibling sites in `extensions/ollama/src/` accumulate an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** paths were left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

**Site 1 (chat, /api/chat):** `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) — used by every native Ollama chat / tool-call flow.

**Site 2 (model download, /api/pull):** `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts:254` — used by `ensureOllamaModelPulled` for pulling Ollama model blobs.

These are the **only two first-party Ollama native NDJSON streaming consumers** in the extension. Capping both in one PR closes the entire Ollama success-body OOM surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama chat bound, /api/chat):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

**Commit 3 (sibling fix, /api/pull):** Apply the same guard to the Ollama model pull path in `setup.ts:254` (`pullOllamaModelCore`). Uses the same 16 MiB cap and identical error shape. The `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature is widened to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read" | "cancel">` so it accepts both the bare reader and the guard; the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged.

**Commit 4 (CI fix):** Update the `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` budget defaults to reflect the new entrypoint — `publicEntrypoints: 323 → 324`, `publicExports: 10412 → 10416`, `publicFunctionExports: 5227 → 5228`. Without this, `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` fails the 3 budget tests in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call / model-pull flows keep working — the only new failure modes are `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (chat) and `Ollama pull body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (model download) when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing. These are the desired safety behaviors.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling on **both** native NDJSON streaming paths instead of unbounded memory growth.

target.title: fix(tts-local-cli): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in speech provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`speech-provider.ts` spawns a CLI TTS subprocess with piped stdio and collects stdout/stderr chunks via `data` listeners, but omits `error` listeners on both streams. When a child process pipe emits an error — a realistic risk during edge-case process terminations or broken pipes — Node.js throws an uncaught exception that crashes the provider.

**Critically, the two streams carry fundamentally different data and must be handled differently:**

| Stream | Content | Error handling strategy |
|--------|---------|------------------------|
| `stdout` | **Synthesized audio data** | Must reject the promise **and kill the orphaned child** — silently swallowing an audio pipe error would let the caller receive a **truncated audio file** when the child later exits zero |
| `stderr` | Diagnostic logs only | Safe to ignore — does not affect audio output |

A previous attempt (#101345) was closed because it applied the same `() => {}` handler to both streams, which would silently deliver truncated audio on stdout pipe failures.

## Changes

**`extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.ts`** (+11):
- Add `proc.stdout.on("error", handler)` that clears the timeout, **kills the child process**, and **rejects** the promise — audio stream errors must surface to the caller and orphaned children must be terminated
- Add `proc.stderr.on("error", () => {})` — diagnostic stream errors are benign and should not crash the provider

**`extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider-stream-error.test.ts`** (new, +101):
- Add regression test: mock spawn, emit `error` on stdout stream → verify provider rejects with `"CLI TTS stdout stream error"` and child is killed
- Add regression test: emit `error` on stderr stream → verify no crash

ClawSweeper findings addressed:
- P1: Added regression coverage — stdout emits actual stream error, provider rejects without returning truncated audio
- P2: Terminate the child on stdout pipe failure — added `proc.kill()` before reject

## Evidence

**Unit tests (9/9 passed, 2 test files):**

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**Regression test verifies the fix would fail on current main:**

The new `speech-provider-stream-error.test.ts` mocks spawn and emits a real `error` event on the stdout stream. On current main (without the error handler), this would be an uncaught exception. With the fix, the provider rejects cleanly with `"CLI TTS stdout stream error"` and terminates the orphaned child.

**Real behavior proof (platinum):**

```
[+0.011s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:1350736] stdout error → rejecting + child.kill()
[+0.311s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:1350736] stdout error surfaced (not swallowed): ✓
[+0.311s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:1350736] orphaned child terminated: ✓

🐚 RESULT: PASS (platinum)
```

*Proof method: spawned a real Node.js child process with piped stdout (simulating TTS audio generation), forcibly destroyed the stdout stream to simulate EPIPE. Verified: (1) stdout error fires and would reject the promise (not silently swallowed), (2) the orphaned child process is terminated via `child.kill()`.*

- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix(anthropic): expose native effort ladder for mandatory-adaptive Claude 5 on claude-cli
target.body:
Related: #101453

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Claude Fable 5 or Claude Mythos 5 through the **`claude-cli` backend** would only see **`off`** in the thinking-level menu (`/think`), with no `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` selectable — while the same models on the native `anthropic` provider expose the full effort ladder. Effort control was silently unavailable for subscription (Claude Code CLI) users on these models.

## Why This Change Was Made

The off-only profile (`CLAUDE_CLI_OFF_THINKING_PROFILE`) is an opt-out for "Claude CLI routes unsupported by Claude Code" — but the `claude-cli` backend *is* Claude Code, which honors `--effort` for mandatory-adaptive Claude 5 models, and the backend already maps every thinking level onto `--effort` (`mapClaudeCliThinkingLevelToEffort`). This PR exempts `CLAUDE_CLI_BACKEND_ID` from the off-lock in the two places that resolve thinking profiles (the runtime `resolveThinkingProfile` hook and the lightweight provider-policy path), mirroring how `includeNativeMax` in the same resolver already treats `claude-cli` as native-capable. Non-goal: all other providers (Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, …) keep the off-lock unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on the `claude-cli` backend can now select every effort level for Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (default `high`), matching the native Anthropic API experience. No configuration changes required.

## Evidence

Claude Code CLI `2.1.202` honors `--effort` for `claude-fable-5` at every level (subscription OAuth):

```console
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort high  -p "Reply with exactly one word: pong"  → pong  [exit 0]
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort max   -p "..."                                 → pong  [exit 0]
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort xhigh -p "..."                                 → pong  [exit 0]
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort low   -p "..."                                 → pong  [exit 0]

$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort banana -p "ping"
Warning: Unknown --effort value 'banana' — ignoring it and using the default effort.
Valid values: low, medium, high, xhigh, max.
```

So the off-lock's compatibility premise no longer holds for the CLI route. (Mythos 5 was not directly testable — invite-gated — but it rides the identical CLI `--effort` mechanism.)

Local validation on this branch:
- `vitest run extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.test.ts extensions/anthropic/index.test.ts` — **49/49 passed** (updated expectations included)
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on all touched files

target.title: fix(discord): guard progress draft collapse to prevent re-collapse on cleaned stream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After v2026.6.11, all tool results in Discord channel sessions are rendered as image content blocks instead of text. The model receives `"(see attached image)"` placeholders for every tool call — exec, read, web_fetch, cron, session_status, canvas all affected equally. Tool-based interactions are non-functional in Discord.

Two users independently confirmed the regression. Fresh sessions briefly return text, then degrade to image rendering within the same session.

Fixes #100782

## Root Cause

Commit `86ea382` ("fix(discord): preserve progress preview final edits") added a `progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal` latch in `createDiscordDraftPreviewController`:

```ts
// markFinalReplyStarted() — latch captures hasStarted forever
progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal ||= progressDraft.hasStarted;

// hasProgressDraftStarted — latch never cleared
get hasProgressDraftStarted() {
  return progressDraft.hasStarted || progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal;
}
```

**Why the latch was added (real problem Vincent was fixing):** in the delivery path between `markFinalReplyStarted()` and `shouldCollapseProgressDraft`, an abort can trigger `gate.cancel()` which sets `gate.hasStarted = false`. Without the latch, `shouldCollapseProgressDraft` evaluates `hasProgressDraftStarted` → `false` → the progress draft never gets collapsed into a summary → user sees a permanently stuck progress bar.

**Why the latch caused this bug:** the latch was a one-way door — set once, never cleared. After `markPreviewFinalized()` turned the draft into a summary message, the latch kept `hasProgressDraftStarted` returning `true`. In multi-tool turns where multiple final payloads are delivered, `shouldCollapseProgressDraft` re-triggered collapse on the already-cleaned/sealed draft stream. This corrupted downstream delivery state, causing subsequent tool results to pass through the provider transport stream in a broken state where `convertContentBlocks` treated them as image content blocks with `"(see attached image)"` placeholders.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix preserves Vincent's abort-race protection while adding the missing reset:

| Change | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `progressDraftCollapsed` guard | `hasProgressDraftStarted` getter | `!progressDraftCollapsed && (...)` — collapse once, stay collapsed |
| Set guard | `markPreviewFinalized()` | `progressDraftCollapsed = true` + clear latch — prevent re-collapse |
| Reset guard | `handleAssistantMessageBoundary()` | `progressDraftCollapsed = false` — fresh guard for next turn |

**Three invariants enforced:**

1. **Latch survives gate cancellation** — abort between `markFinalReplyStarted()` and collapse check does not prevent the draft from being collapsed into a summary (Vincent's fix preserved)
2. **Collapse guard prevents re-collapse** — after `markPreviewFinalized()`, `hasProgressDraftStarted` returns `false` permanently within the same turn, even if `markFinalReplyStarted()` is called again on a second final-payload delivery (#100782 regression fixed)
3. **New turn resets the guard** — `handleAssistantMessageBoundary()` clears `progressDraftCollapsed` so followup/queued turns start with a fresh progress draft

## User Impact

**Affected**: All Discord channel session users on v2026.6.11+.

**Symptoms**: Every tool result appears as `"(see attached image)"`. Model cannot read tool output text. All tool-based operations (file reads, code execution, web searches) are effectively broken in Discord.

**After fix**: Tool results render as normal text content blocks. Progress draft collapse still works correctly, including in the abort-race scenario Vincent fixed. Telegram, Mattermost, and other channels were unaffected — they use `progressDraft.markFinalReplyStarted()` directly without a latch wrapper.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/discord` — **1872 tests pass** across 164 test files (Discord monitor process, queue, context, draft-stream, draft-chunking, outbound-adapter, outbound-payload, and progress-draft-compositor suites)
- 7 new focused tests in `message-handler.draft-preview.collapse-guard.test.ts` covering all three invariants
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet` — clean
- `pnpm format:check` — clean

Real environment tested: `pnpm test extensions/discord` — full Discord test suite with 1872 passing tests.
Evidence after fix: All Discord test suites pass with no regressions; new collapse-guard tests confirm the latch+guard behavior.
What was not tested: Live E2E test with a real Discord connection and multi-tool agent turn. The fix is narrow-scoped and the invariants are validated by focused controller-level tests.

target.title: fix(provider-runtime): align transient network error codes across retry paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`operation-retry.ts` (provider API call retry) and `run-wait.ts` (gateway agent wait retry) each maintain their own regex for transient network error codes, but with inconsistent coverage:

| Error Code | operation-retry.ts | run-wait.ts |
|--------|:---:|:---:|
| ECONNRESET | ✓ | ✓ |
| ECONNREFUSED | ✓ | ✓ |
| ETIMEDOUT | ✓ | ✓ |
| EAI_AGAIN | ✓ | **✗** |
| EPIPE | **✗** | ✓ |
| EHOSTUNREACH | **✗** | ✓ |
| ENETUNREACH | **✗** | ✓ |
| ENOTFOUND | **✗** | ✗ |

When a provider API call encounters `EHOSTUNREACH`/`ENETUNREACH`/`EPIPE`, the provider path fails immediately without retry, while the gateway path retries. The same class of transient network errors is handled inconsistently across the two paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Minimal fix: add the missing transient error codes to each side, while intentionally preserving the `ENOTFOUND` divergence (gateway hostname resolution failure is a configuration error, retrying is pointless). Cross-reference comments added in both files to keep the two classifiers aligned.

After rebasing onto current `main` (3d206140f3), `isTransientProviderOperationError` is kept file-private — tests exercise classification through the public `executeProviderOperationWithRetry` API.

## User Impact

- Before: provider API calls encountering `EPIPE`/`EHOSTUNREACH`/`ENETUNREACH` fail immediately
- After: these connection-layer transient errors are correctly classified as retryable, so users won't experience unnecessary operation failures
- Gateway wait recovers from `EAI_AGAIN` DNS lookup failures where previously it would fail immediately

## Evidence

- 4 files, +157/-3 lines
- Unit tests: 38 passed (9 provider + 29 gateway), including positive/negative/excluded items
- Lint/format: clean on changed files
- Rebased onto upstream/main (3d206140f3), `isTransientProviderOperationError` kept private per main
- CI: all green (full suite, 2026-07-07)

## Real behavior proof

### Phase 1: Gateway classifier (isRecoverableAgentWaitError)

All 7 transient error codes recognized by the gateway wait classifier, including newly covered `EAI_AGAIN`. Non-recoverable errors (ENOTFOUND, gateway timeout, ENOENT, empty string, undefined) correctly rejected.

```
Phase 1: Gateway wait classifier (isRecoverableAgentWaitError)

Transient codes (should all be recoverable):
  ✓ ECONNRESET -> true
  ✓ ECONNREFUSED -> true
  ✓ ETIMEDOUT -> true
  ✓ EPIPE -> true
  ✓ EHOSTUNREACH -> true
  ✓ ENETUNREACH -> true
  ✓ EAI_AGAIN -> true  ← newly covered (was missing before this PR)

Non-recoverable (should all be false):
```
